records.description:
### **Job Title**

Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities

### **Job Description**

Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities

The Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities is responsible for overseeing the strategic management of the QMS department, aligning it with organizational goals and industry best practices. The role formulates and implements QMS strategies to drive continuous improvement and ensures high standards of quality and compliance. The role oversees the analysis of complex QMS data and trends across multiple functions to identify systemic issues, leads cross-functional teams in root cause analysis, and drives the implementation of strategic quality improvement initiatives.

**Your role:**

* Oversees the strategic direction and management of the QMS department, aligning it with organizational goals, company policies, and industry best practices. Partners with senior leadership so that quality strategy supports operational efficiency, risk management, and business growth.
* Supports QMS functions such as document control, internal audits, CAPA, and training, ensuring effective implementation, compliance, and continuous improvement. Drives advanced training and competency programs, and keeps current on quality standards, to promote organization-wide adherence and continuous learning.
* Analyzes complex QMS data and trends across functions to identify systemic issues and leads cross-functional teams in root cause analysis and strategic quality improvement initiatives. Develops and maintains quality metrics and reports to track QMS performance and keep management informed.
* Leads quality risk management frameworks and advises executive leadership on regulatory changes, compliance risks, and quality trends. Represents the organization in industry forums, regulatory discussions, and quality committees to share best practices and help shape future standards.
Facilitates strategic cross-functional collaboration to resolve high-impact quality issues and align with organizational quality objectives. Owns planning, staffing, budgeting, and priorities, and leads succession planning and talent management, including selection, performance, compensation, and career development. 

 

**You're the right fit if:**

* You’ve acquired 15+ years of experience in Quality Management Systems, Quality Audits or equivalent in industry areas such as Medical Device, Pharmaceutical, or Biotech. 7+ years of people leadership experience managing teams of direct reports.
* Your skills include strategic Director-level leadership, independent decision-making, and the ability to lead experienced technical teams in a global, FDA-regulated environment. Your skills include enterprise QMS technology leadership, system validation, regulatory compliance, vendor management, and quality-system modernization across platforms such as Veeva, Windchill, and ARIS.
* You have a Bachelor’s/master’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent.
* You must be able to successfully perform the following minimum Physical, Cognitive and Environmental job requirements with or without accommodation for this position .
You’re an independent, strategic leader who navigates ambiguity with confidence, makes sound decisions, and builds trust across experienced teams and global stakeholders. You must be willing and able to travel up to 10%. 

**How we work together**

We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

This is an office-based role.

**About Philips**

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

* **Learn more about** **our business** **.**
* **Discover** **our rich and exciting history.**
* **Learn more about** **our purpose.**
* **Learn more about** **our culture.**

**Philips Transparency Details**

The pay range for this position in Murrysville, PA or Nashville, TN is $162,000 to $258,000.

The pay range for this position in Plymouth, MN is $170,000 to $270,000.

The pay range for this position in Cambridge, MA is $181,000 to $288,000.

The actual base pay offered may vary within the posted ranges depending on multiple factors including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

In addition, other compensation, such as an annual incentive bonus, sales commission or long-term incentives may be offered. Employees are eligible to participate in our comprehensive Philips Total Rewards benefits program, which includes a generous PTO, 401k (up to 7% match), HSA (with company contribution), stock purchase plan, education reimbursement and much more. Details about our benefits can be found here .

At Philips, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top end of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

**Additional Information**

US work authorization is a precondition of employment. The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa, now or in the future.

Company relocation benefits **will not** be provided for this position. For this position, you must reside in **or** within commuting distance to posted locations **.**

#LI-PH1

 
 
 

This requisition is expected to stay active for 45 days but may close earlier if a successful candidate is selected or business necessity dictates. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure consideration.

*Philips is an Equal Employment and Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets and maintains a drug-free workplace.*

records.title: Senior Director, Quality
records.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53236
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/Executive Director of Quality for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/Executive Director of Quality leads all aspects of site Quality Control and Quality Assurance operations including QA Operations, QA Systems, QA Validation, and QC. In this role you’ll lead the site quality system and culture, batch disposition, and inspection readiness. This role owns and manages all regulatory inspections; and represents the site’s conduit for quality metrics, quality system work, and transformational quality strategy to bring Regeneron to best-in-class lean quality operations. They will oversee and preserve our quality independence from operational pressure while partnering closely with site leadership.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own the site quality system (both QA &QC) and lead a culture of compliance, accountability, and right-first-time execution

* + QA: ops, systems, and validation owned directly alongside QC as part of a unified site quality organization

* + QC: responsible for delivering utilities, in-process and release testing, performing environmental monitoring, QC laboratory compliance, and method transfer support that enable timely, compliant batch release

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary party responsible for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Hold batch disposition authority, ensuring compliance and timely batch release

* Own and manage all regulatory inspections ensuring the site is continuously inspection-ready and leading the site through regulatory agency inspections and customer and corporate audits

* Serve as the site's primary conduit for quality metrics, quality system work, and l quality strategy connecting site execution to enterprise quality’s vision for best-in-class lean quality operations

* Provide governance of laboratory investigations, deviations, and CAPA management across all quality sub-functions

* Lead all aspects of batch record review and disposition support, floor quality presence, and deviation management for manufacturing for Saratoga Site

* Lead all aspects of QMS administration, document control, training compliance, CAPA system administration, and audit readiness for Saratoga Site

* Build and coordinate best-in-class validation programs process, cleaning, and equipment validation grounded in FDA's three-stage process validation lifecycle (Stage 1 Process Design, Stage 2 Process Qualification/PPQ, Stage 3 Continued Process Verification), EU Annex 15, ASTM E2500 risk-based qualification, and ICH Q8–Q11 Quality by Design principles tailored to large-molecule biotech manufacturing, including PPQ support for new suite introduction

* Lead quality readiness for suites entering service, including validation, qualification, and quality system scale-up

* Partner with manufacturing, technical services, technical operations, and supply chain as a core member of the site leadership team

* Own quality's role in the digital and connected plant model, including electronic quality systems, review by exception, and data integrity by design

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing quality organization; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

* Lead a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance

* Own and manage the site’s data governance program, including data integrity standards, data ownership and accountability, lifecycle controls, and periodic review, so data is reliable from the floor to leadership reporting

* Own and manage the site’s quality management maturity, including assessing current state against enterprise and industry benchmarks, setting the improvement roadmap, and driving measurable gains in quality system performance

* Own and manage the site’s contamination control strategy, including its design, governance, and day-to-day execution across facility, equipment, process, personnel, and materials, with ongoing trending and review of effectiveness
 

 
 

**This role requires:**

* B.S in Life Sciences, Engineering, or a related technical field

records.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 6 Dec 2026 
 

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

**A Day in the Life**
=====================

At Medtronic, you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world. We work with a sense of purpose and ownership, knowing there is a human life on the other side of every decision.
 
 
In this enterprise leadership role, the Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality will advance Design and Development excellence across Medtronic by shaping strategy, standards, governance, and enterprise capability for Design Quality and product development processes. Supporting every Medtronic Operating Unit and product category, this leader will drive consistency, strengthen Design Control execution, improve organizational capability, and help teams successfully navigate complex product development challenges.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings deep Design Quality and product development expertise, strong technical credibility, and a demonstrated track record of leading through complexity to deliver business, quality, and patient-focused outcomes. This individual will be a trusted enterprise partner who collaborates across Operating Units, Core Quality Services, and executive leadership teams to remove barriers, accelerate progress, and enable innovation while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and patient safety.
 
 
At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person collaboration is critical to the success of this enterprise leadership role. This position requires an on-site presence a minimum of four days per week and must be based at one of the Medtronic U.S. campuses listed below. 

**Work Location**

This position will be onsite and based at one of the following Medtronic locations in the contiguous United States:

* Mounds View, MN / Minneapolis, MN (Twin Cities Campus)
* Irvine, CA / Santa Ana, CA (Orange County Campus)
* Lafayette, CO (Colorado Campus)
* Greater Boston Area (Boston, Danvers, or Mansfield, MA)
* North Haven, CT
* Memphis, TN
* Fort Worth, TX
* Jacksonville, FL
* Tempe, AZ

Travel up to 20% is required.

 

As **Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality** , you will provide enterprise leadership for Design Quality across Medtronic's global portfolio of medical technologies. You will partner with Operating Unit, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Product Development, and executive leaders to strengthen Design and Development practices, improve Design Control effectiveness, and enable successful execution across a diverse range of products and technologies.

You will serve as a highly credible Design Quality leader and trusted advisor, helping teams solve complex product development challenges while driving strategic initiatives that improve quality outcomes, product safety, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

Success in this role requires the ability to influence across a highly matrixed organization while maintaining a hands-on approach that removes barriers and accelerates execution. You will lead a small team of experts while driving enterprise-wide impact through collaboration, technical leadership, and capability building.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

 

***Lead enterprise Design Quality strategy, standards, and governance.***

* Develop and execute the enterprise Design Quality strategy, governance model, standards, and service priorities across Medtronic's global product portfolio.
* Establish and maintain enterprise Design Quality standards that enable consistent execution, regulatory readiness, and risk-based decision making.
* Own enterprise Design Quality process health, KPI visibility, and performance management mechanisms to identify trends, elevate risks, and drive timely action.
Create and lead governance mechanisms supporting critical product development programs, including escalation, issue resolution, and cross-functional decision making. 

***Drive enterprise initiatives and cross-functional partnerships that improve product development effectiveness, quality, and patient safety.***

* Partner with Operating Unit development teams to address complex design and development challenges through technical consultation, coaching, and expert guidance.
* Drive enterprise initiatives focused on improving product development effectiveness, product quality, patient safety, and risk management.
* Lead and influence strategic initiatives across the DRM Council, Productivity Workstream, Software Excellence Workstream, Global Operations & Supply Chain (GOSC), and Core Quality Services.
* Advance enterprise priorities, including Predicate Product Risk Reduction (PPRR) and other high-impact Design Quality improvement initiatives.
Partner with other Quality Centers of Excellence, including Risk Management, CAPA, and Acquisitions, to ensure alignment across critical quality processes. 

***Serve as the enterprise Design Quality expert, building capability and influencing critical decisions.***

* Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for Design Quality, Design Controls, and Design & Development excellence.
* Build enterprise Design Quality capability through coaching, mentoring, talent development, and deployment of best practices.
* Influence decisions with potential enterprise-wide impact involving product safety, compliance, regulatory risk, legal exposure, business performance, and Medtronic's reputation.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, technical excellence, continuous improvement, and patient focus. 

 

**Must Have: Minimum Requirements**

 

**To be considered for this role, please ensure the minimum requirements are evident on your resume.**

* Bachelor's degree required and 10+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles **OR** Advanced degree with 8+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles.
* Minimum of 7 years of people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design Quality and Design Control activities within regulated medical device, software, combination product, or similarly regulated industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design & Development, Design Quality, or Product Development initiatives across multiple business units, product platforms, or enterprise functions within a complex, matrixed organization.
Experience supporting the development, design transfer, or lifecycle management of regulated medical technologies. 

 

**Nice to Have**

 

***Product development and Design Quality experience across the lifecycle.***

* Extensive experience serving on product development Core Teams through multiple phases of the product lifecycle.
* Demonstrated success leading complex product development or Design Quality challenges across diverse technologies and product categories.
Experience leading enterprise-wide quality, product development, or transformation initiatives across multiple business units. 

***Deep technical, regulatory, and digital expertise.***

* Deep expertise in Design Controls, Design Verification and Validation, Risk Management, and Design & Development processes.
* Strong knowledge of FDA regulations, QMSR, ISO 13485, EU MDR, GMP, and other global regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting software-enabled medical technologies, digital health products, combination products, or other complex regulated technologies.
Experience leveraging analytics, AI-enabled tools, automation, and digital technologies to improve quality performance and organizational effectiveness. 

***Leadership through influence in a highly matrixed environment.***

* Proven ability to build alignment and influence decision-making among technical experts, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
* Demonstrated success leading through influence in a highly matrixed environment while delivering large-scale organizational impact.
* Hands-on leadership style with a demonstrated ability to remove barriers, accelerate execution, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

**Physical Job Requirements**

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position.

The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role.

**U.S. Work Authorization & Sponsorship**

At Medtronic, we are committed to fostering an environment where employees can thrive and make a meaningful impact. In alignment with our enterprise-wide workforce planning approach, U.S. work authorization sponsorship (H-1B, TN, J, etc.) is offered exclusively for Principal-level roles and above, where specialized expertise aligns with long-term business needs. Roles below the Principal level require candidates to possess unrestricted U.S. work authorization at the time of hire and for the duration of employment.
‌

**Recruitment Fraud Alert**

We are aware of phishing scams targeting job seekers. Please keep the following in mind:

 

Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic.com email addresses.

 

Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate.

 

If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Medtronic, do not respond, click links, or open attachments.

 

If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic.com .
‌

**Benefits & Compensation**
===========================

**Medtronic offers a competitive Salary and flexible Benefits Package** 
A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values. We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help to create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every career and life stage.

Salary ranges for U.S (excl. PR) locations (USD):$184,000.00 - $276,000.00
‌ 
This position is eligible for a short-term incentive called the Medtronic Incentive Plan (MIP).The base salary range is applicable across the United States, excluding Puerto Rico and specific locations in California. The offered rate complies with federal and local regulations and may vary based on factors such as experience, certification/education, market conditions, and location. Compensation and benefits information pertains solely to candidates hired within the United States (local market compensation and benefits will apply for others).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to those regular employees who work 20+ hours per week: Health, Dental and vision insurance , Health Savings Account , Healthcare Flexible Spending Account , Life insurance, Long-term disability leave , Dependent daycare spending account , Tuition assistance/reimbursement , and Simple Steps (global well-being program).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to all regular employees: Incentive plans, 401(k) plan plus employer contribution and match , Short-term disability , Paid time off , Paid holidays , Employee Stock Purchase Plan , Employee Assistance Program , Non-qualified Retirement Plan Supplement (subject to IRS earning minimums) , and Capital Accumulation Plan (available to Vice Presidents and above, or subject to IRS earning minimums).

Regular employees are those who are not temporary, such as interns. Temporary employees are eligible for paid sick time, as required under applicable state law, and the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Please note some of the above benefits may not apply to workers in Puerto Rico.

Further details are available at the link below:

Medtronic benefits and compensation plans

It is the policy of Medtronic to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, Medtronic will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

 

If you are applying to perform work for Medtronic, Inc. (“Medtronic”) in any position which will involve performing at least two (2) hours of work on average each week within the unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County, you can find here a list of all material job duties of the specific job position which Medtronic reasonably believes that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment. Medtronic will consider for employment qualified job applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.

records.title: Director, Quality Compliance (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
records.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Compliance provides strategic and operational leadership for critical compliance activities across the medical device organization. This role leads regulatory inspection readiness, product issue escalation and compliance risk assessment, regulatory agency responses, correction and removal activities, and large-scale compliance improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Director serves as a senior compliance partner to Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and business leadership, ensuring significant quality and compliance issues are rapidly assessed, appropriately escalated, and effectively resolved. The position requires strong judgment, executive communication, and the ability to lead complex, cross-functional activities in a highly regulated environment.
 
 
Beyond compliance subject-matter leadership, the Director owns the compliance function's budget and resourcing, shapes its organizational strategy and structure, and contributes to broader business planning — balancing business objectives with compliance risk and representing the function in strategic and operational business reviews. The Director leads a global team of regional compliance specialists, building organizational capability across all manufacturing sites and functions.



**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Organizational Strategy & Business Leadership

* Shape the multi-year strategy and organizational design for the compliance function, including workforce planning, capability building, and succession planning.

* Lead, develop, and manage a global team of compliance professionals, including direct oversight of regional compliance specialists across manufacturing sites.

* Partner with business, Quality, and Regulatory leadership to align compliance priorities with broader business strategy, product roadmaps, and operational plans.

* Represent the compliance organization in business planning, budget reviews, and strategic planning forums, providing a compliance-risk perspective to business decisions.

* Build organizational capability and structure to scale the compliance function as the business grows.

Inspection Readiness

* Establish and maintain an enterprise inspection-readiness program supporting regulatory inspections and other external assessments.

* Lead inspection preparation, including readiness assessments, mock inspections, documentation reviews, front-room/back-room preparation, subject-matter-expert coaching, and inspection logistics.

* Identify systemic readiness gaps and drive corrective actions to improve sustained inspection preparedness.

* Develop inspection-readiness metrics, lessons learned, and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

Product Issue Escalation & Risk Assessment

* Lead or facilitate cross-functional assessments of significant product quality, safety, compliance, and regulatory issues requiring senior-level escalation.

* Ensure emerging product issues are evaluated using structured, documented risk-based decision-making.

* Partner with Medical Safety, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, Operations, and other functions to evaluate product and compliance risk and determine appropriate escalation and response.

* Provide independent compliance challenge and guidance when significant product-related decisions could create regulatory or patient-safety implications.

* Ensure escalated issues have clear ownership, documented rationale, timely decisions, and appropriate executive visibility.

Regulatory Agency Responses

* Lead the development and coordination of responses to regulatory inspection observations, agency inquiries, compliance correspondence, and other significant regulatory matters.

* Establish cross-functional response teams, governance, deliverables, and escalation mechanisms.

* Ensure responses are factually supported, internally consistent, appropriately reviewed, and supported by sustainable corrective actions.

* Monitor commitments made to regulatory authorities through completion and verify appropriate evidence of implementation and effectiveness.

* Provide senior leadership with clear assessments of response status, risks, dependencies, and potential compliance exposure.

Correction & Removal Oversight and Execution

* Provide oversight and leadership for product corrections and removals, including recalls and field actions, in partnership with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other relevant functions.

* Lead governance and execution for complex or high-risk correction and removal activities.

* Ensure decisions are supported by appropriate health-hazard, quality, regulatory, and compliance risk assessments.

* Establish clear accountability for affected-product identification, communications, execution, reconciliation, effectiveness monitoring, and closure.

* Monitor significant field actions through completion and escalate implementation risks or unexpected trends to senior leadership.

* Drive lessons learned and systemic improvements following significant product actions.

Large-Scale Compliance Improvement Projects

* Lead enterprise or multi-site compliance remediation and improvement programs involving significant regulatory, quality-system, or business risk.

* Translate regulatory observations, internal audit findings, systemic quality issues, or emerging compliance risks into structured remediation strategies and executable workstreams.

* Establish program governance, accountability, milestones, risk management, escalation processes, and executive reporting.

* Coordinate activities across functions and sites to ensure remediation addresses underlying systemic issues rather than isolated symptoms.

* Evaluate implementation progress and evidence of effectiveness to support sustainable closure.

* Serve as a compliance leader for major transformation initiatives involving quality-system processes, governance, controls, or organizational capabilities.

Leadership & Governance Responsibilities

* Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on significant compliance and regulatory risks.

* Provide independent compliance perspective during complex or high-risk decision-making.

* Establish governance mechanisms that enable timely escalation, transparent risk communication, and clear accountability.

* Develop organizational capability in inspection readiness, regulatory response, issue escalation, and compliance risk management.

* Promote a culture of proactive risk identification, regulatory accountability, patient safety, and sustainable compliance.

* Mentor and develop compliance professionals and cross-functional leaders involved in regulatory and remediation activities.

* Partner with business leadership on budget planning and resource allocation decisions affecting the compliance organization.

 

**Qualifications Required**
---------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, quality, regulatory affairs, or a related discipline and 12+ years’ industry experience.

* Significant progressive experience in Quality, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, or related functions within the medical device or similarly regulated life-sciences industry.

* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading regulatory inspections and inspection readiness.

* Experience managing significant product quality or compliance escalations and structured risk assessments.

* Experience developing or coordinating responses to regulatory authorities.

* Strong working knowledge of medical-device quality-system and post-market regulatory requirements.

* Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional compliance or remediation programs.

* Experience managing budgets, resource planning, or organizational design within a compliance, quality, or regulatory function.

* Demonstrated business acumen, with the ability to balance business objectives and compliance risk in decision-making.

* Prior people leadership experience, including managing geographically distributed teams, strongly preferred.

* Strong executive communication, judgment, influence, and problem-solving skills.

 

**Core Competencies**
---------------------

* Regulatory and compliance strategy

* Organizational strategy and workforce planning

* Budget and resource management

* Business acumen and strategic planning

* Inspection management and readiness

* Product and compliance risk assessment

* Regulatory agency communication

* Correction and removal governance

* Quality-system remediation

* Program and project leadership

* Executive-level communication

* Cross-functional influence

* Critical decision-making under pressure

* Root-cause and systemic problem solving

* Change leadership

Additional Information:



Compensation & Benefits:

For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $172,400.00 - $258,575.00

This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid time off (PTO)
• And additional employee wellness programs

Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
 
 
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

At Insulet Corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

### **POSITION****SUMMARY:**

Working closely with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team, the Director of Program Quality and Training of Youth Programs documents best practices, designs tools to measure staff and youth outcomes, and supports collaboration among youth-serving organizations. This role provides strategic leadership for quality improvement, staff development, and outcomes assessment across Cambridge Youth Programs’ five youth centers serving more than 1,200 youth ages 9–19, partnering with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team to codify best practices, build measurement tools, and strengthen collaboration among youth-serving organizations. The Director directly supervises an Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector, and manages organization-wide partnerships, grant implementation and reporting, and recruitment and outreach efforts.

### **ESSENTIAL****JOB****FUNCTIONS****and****DUTIES:**

*The**essential**functions**or**duties**listed**below**are**intended**only**as**illustrations**of**the**various**type**of**work**that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Support expanded learning and out-of-school-time programs serving youth ages 9–19 across the City’s youth centers, including afterschool programs, evening programs, school vacation programming, and specialized youth activities.
* Assist the Division Head for Youth Programs in establishing program goals, objectives, and operational priorities.
* Assist with oversight of programs and activities across the City’s youth centers and collaborate with

 Youth Program staff as part of the Cambridge Youth Programs Leadership Team.
* Provide strategic oversight and support for program quality improvement initiatives and develop systems to assess, track, and manage program performance using positive youth development principles.
* Develop and implement systems to identify staff training and professional development needs and design and deliver training programs that support best practices in youth development, out-of-school-time programming, and effective supervision.
* Provide guidance and support to program staff in program planning, implementation, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop and manage organization-wide partnerships, initiatives, and grant partnerships, including implementation oversight and grant reporting; support recruitment materials development and outreach to prospective participants and partner organizations.
* Supervise a Youth Connector who develops and supports sites around middle school and teen transition programs, pre-teen, middle school, and teen recruitment and enrollment, and the organization’s social media plan.
* Provide direct coaching support to assigned youth center sites, working with Program Directors on a weekly basis to develop, implement, and assess both site-based plans and collective projects across the organization.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations to design and implement tools that measure staff and youth outcomes, support organizational accountability, and evaluate program effectiveness.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations, develop, coordinate, and manage staff trainings and professional development for full-time and part-time staff.
* Conduct program evaluations, analyze data, and prepare quarterly reports that support performance measurement and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support collaboration and resource sharing among youth centers, schools, community organizations, families, and public safety partners.
* Perform related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Education/Experience***

* A bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a related field; master’s degree preferred.
* Three (3) years of out-of-school time (OST) program management experience required.
* Five (5) years of experience supervising staff and working with diverse populations required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of positive youth development principles and experience in program development required.
* Experience developing and implementing systems for program delivery, staff training, program quality improvement, evaluation, and assessment processes.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without direct line authority and provide leadership in developing and sustaining collaborative internal and external partnerships.
* Experience working with community agencies, youth, and schools required.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, presentation, writing, organizational, and facilitation skills required.
* An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant lived or professional experience may be considered.

***Knowledge,******Skills,******and*** ***Abilities:***
-------------------------------------------------------

* Deep knowledge of positive youth development, out-of-school time program models, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive practices.
* Skill in designing, facilitating, and evaluating staff training using adult learning principles, coaching strategies, and reflective supervision techniques.
* Ability to develop and implement program quality frameworks and assessment tools and use qualitative and quantitative data to support continuous improvement efforts.
* Strong facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to convene diverse stakeholders and lead collaborative problem-solving initiatives across multiple sites.
* Proficiency with data management, project management, and budgeting tools and systems.
* Ability to manage complex projects, timelines, and competing priorities while ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, and leadership skills with the ability to build and sustain collaborative partnerships.
* Commitment to anti-racism, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
* Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

### **SUPERVISION****RECEIVED:**

### **Works****under****the****general****direction****of****the****Division****Head****of****Cambridge****Youth****Programs;****exercises****considerable independent judgment; and has work reviewed through conferences, reports, and achievement of program** **objectives.**

### 

### **SUPERVISION****EXERCISED:**

### **May****directly****supervise****two full-time staff members:****an****Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector.****Also provides functional supervision and coaching support to Program Directors and staff across assigned youth center sites; may oversee consultants or interns engaged in training, program quality, and evaluation** **initiatives.**

### 

### **WORK** **ENVIRONMENT:**

### **Work is performed in a standard office setting with fluorescent lighting, carpeted floors, air conditioning, and moderate noise levels. Evening and weekend hours may be required to support operational needs.**

### 

### **PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:**

### **Ability****to****use****a****computer****to****access,****input,****and****retrieve****information;****answer****telephones;****maintain****multiple****files; and lift items weighing up to 25 pounds. Ability to travel throughout the City of Cambridge to multiple Youth Center locations as required.**

*The City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to**work and interact**effectively**with**individuals**and**groups**with**a variety of**identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.*

**COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY**

The City of Cambridge is committed to providing fair, transparent, and competitive compensation to all employees. The salary range listed in this job posting reflects the full range for this position's pay grade (Steps 1–10). New employees joining the organization are hired within the hiring range, Steps 1 through 5, with placement at the midpoint reserved for the most qualified candidates. Starting placement is based on directly related education and experience relative to the minimum qualifications of the position, required licenses or certifications, internal equity with current employees, and relevant labor market factors. Employees progress through the 10 steps over time through the City's established step and pay progression policies.

This compensation philosophy applies to non‑union positions. For union positions, please refer to the applicable collective bargaining agreement.

Current City employees applying to another position should refer to the Compensation & Classification Manual for the policies governing promotions, lateral transfers, and other internal salary changes.

**ABOUT THE CITY OF CAMBRIDGE**

The City of Cambridge is a diverse and vibrant community that 120,000 residents of different ethnic, racial, religious, U.S. nationals and other backgrounds call home. We take pride in our City’s diversity and strive to create a workplace that is reflective of the community we serve - one in which all employees can thrive. The City is also deeply committed to creating an environment in which all our employees are treated equitably and feel included. In joining our team, you would work in a workplace environment that advances and values antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion (ADEI), and that is committed to embedding ADEI best practices and tenets in all aspects of our work. City of Cambridge residents are especially encouraged to apply to job openings.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY / AFFIRMATIVE ACTION**

The City of Cambridge is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, sex, religion, age, national origin, disability, or any other protected category. Women, minorities, veterans, members of the LGBTQ+ Community, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. The City is committed to advancing a workforce culture of antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Auxiliary aids and services, written materials in alternative formats, and reasonable modifications in policies and procedures will be provided to qualified individuals with disabilities free of charge, upon request by contacting Human Resources at humanresources@cambridgema.gov.

records.description:
**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264366 **Date posted** 19/11/2026

 

**WHY JOIN US?**

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by **engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week**. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.**This is a hybrid role located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Candidates must reside within commuting distance of Gaithersburg or be willing to relocate for this opportunity.****About the Role**

The Director, Quality Systems is a senior leader within Development Quality Biologics (DQB), accountable for strategy, governance, performance, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS) supporting Biologics Development.

The role provides leadership and oversight for critical Quality Systems processes, including Deviation and CAPA Management, Change Control, Quality Risk Management, Inspection Management, Documentation Management, Quality Management Review, and GxP Training and Learning. The Director also leads Business Process Management (BPM) within DQB, ensuring business and quality processes are effectively owned, defined, governed, measured, and continuously improved.

The Director leads a team of up to 12 employees and partners broadly across DQB, Biopharmaceutical Development (BPD), Development Quality, Global Quality, and other functions to deliver a compliant, efficient, risk-based, and future-ready QMS.

**Key Accountabilities**

* Lead the DQB Quality Management System, providing strategy, governance, and oversight to ensure Quality Systems are compliant, effective, risk-based, phase-appropriate, and fit for purpose.

* Provide leadership for core Quality Systems processes, including deviations and CAPAs, change control, quality risk management, inspection management and readiness, documentation management, Quality Management Review, GxP training, and associated metrics and trending. Champion excellence in fundamental Quality processes like root cause analysis and effective CAPA development, risk mitigation, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.

* Lead Business Process Management within DQB, establishing clear process ownership, governance, performance measures, and improvement mechanisms. Drive simplification, standardization, and elimination of non-value-added activities while maintaining appropriate compliance and control.

* Drive QMS performance and continuous improvement through meaningful metrics, trending, management review, risk identification, and data-driven insights. Translate QMS performance into clear priorities and actions for DQB and BPD leadership.

* Ensure sustainable inspection readiness, including effective preparation, execution, response, and follow-up for regulatory inspections and audits, ensuring learnings are incorporated into Quality System improvements.

* Lead and develop a team of up to 12 employees, building capability in Quality Systems, process ownership, risk-based decision-making, data and digital fluency, continuous improvement, and critical thinking.

**Shaping the QMS of the Future**

The Director will play a key role in evolving the DQB QMS to support the future needs of the Biologics’ development portfolio and AZ's 2030 Vision. The role will champion a phase-appropriate, risk-based and digitally enabled QMS that is fit for purpose, reduces unnecessary complexity, enables innovation, and maintains strong regulatory compliance and patient-focused quality.

The Director role will lead the responsible adoption of AI, advanced analytics, automation, digital workflows, and other emerging technologies to simplify processes, reduce manual work, improve knowledge access, identify quality signals earlier, and strengthen data-driven decision-making. The role will help advance the QMS from primarily retrospective management of quality events toward a more proactive and predictive model, while ensuring appropriate human accountability, transparency, data integrity, traceability, and GxP controls.

**Measures of Success**

**Success in the role will be demonstrated through:**

* A compliant, effective, phase-appropriate, and fit-for-purpose QMS that enables delivery of the AZ portfolio.

* Strong QMS health, including effective management of deviations, CAPAs, changes, risks, training, documentation, and inspection readiness.

* Mature Business Process Management with clear accountability and measurable improvements in process effectiveness, efficiency, and simplicity.

* A Quality Management Review with processes and metrics that provide actionable insights, identify emerging risks, and enable timely leadership decisions.

* Increased and appropriately governed use of data, digital solutions, automation, and AI to improve QMS performance and reduce administrative burden.

* A capable, engaged team prepared to lead and support the QMS of the future.

**Essential Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or technical discipline such as Pharmacy, Biology, Chemistry, Biotechnology, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience within Quality in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading a sizeable (10+) Quality team/function and delivering measurable improvements.
* Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including deviations/CAPA, change control, Quality Risk Management, documentation, training, and inspection readiness.
* Strong understanding of GxP requirements, regulatory expectations, and SOP-driven environments, with experience driving compliance and sustainable Quality practices.
* Experience using Quality metrics, trending, risk indicators, and management review to identify priorities and drive continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives and significant process or organizational change, including management of resources, stakeholders, vendors, and budgets.
* Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to partner across Quality, Development, and senior leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience within biologics, Development Quality, or pharmaceutical development.
* Experience managing managers or leading leaders within a Quality organization.
* Experience with Business Process Management, Operational Excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement.
* Experience leading QMS transformation, harmonization, or process simplification.
* Experience with digital Quality systems, automation, advanced analytics, or AI-enabled Quality solutions in a regulated environment.
* Experience with non-GMP biopharmaceutical work and its phase-appropriate requirements for compliance.

**SO, WHAT’S NEXT?**

To be considered for this exciting opportunity, please complete the full application on our website at your earliest convenience – it is the only way that our Recruiter and Hiring Manager can know that you feel well qualified for this opportunity. If you know someone who would be a great fit, please share this posting with them.

**Are you interested in working at AZ, apply today!**

AstraZeneca is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion and providing a workplace that is free from discrimination. AstraZeneca is committed to accommodating persons with disabilities. Such accommodation is available on request in respect of all aspects of the recruitment, assessment and selection process and may be requested by emailing AZCHumanResources@astrazeneca.com.

#LI-Hybrid

*The annual base pay for this position ranges from $174,856.80 - $229,499.55 USD. Base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.*

*In addition, our positions offer a short-term incentive bonus opportunity; eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program. Benefits offered included a qualified retirement program [401(k) plan]; paid vacation and holidays; paid leaves; and, health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans.*

*Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base pay (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.*

records.description:
**About Us:**

BW Design Group is a fully integrated architecture, engineering, construction, system integration, and consulting firm committed to helping our clients realize their most critical goals from Strategy to Commercialization. As the only firm born from a manufacturing technology company to become an independent and fully integrated firm, we combine deep domain expertise in the manufacturing environment with an approach that is built to serve the dynamic needs of our clients. Rooted in our distinct culture of Truly Human Leadership, we cultivate the leaders who will define tomorrow and partner with our clients in the food & beverage, life sciences, industrial, and advanced technology industries to build the future of manufacturing and technology. 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world. 
 

**Job Description:**

**Who You’ll Work With**

At BW Design Group, you'll collaborate with experienced leaders, technical specialists, and subject matter experts to solve complex challenges for some of the world's leading companies. You'll join a growing team of more than 2000 professionals across nearly 50 U.S. offices where you'll be empowered to make an impact, develop your expertise, and grow your career.

As Director, Quality for our Boston office, you will join our Regulatory Compliance Practice, leading the local quality team while serving as a trusted quality subject matter expert, industry thought leader, and client lead for life science clients across New England.

**What You’ll Do**

This role balances hands-on, billable project/service delivery with growing our Boston team, client relationships, and reputation in the industry.

* Lead a team of quality professionals and interface with clients
* Train, mentor, and recruit talent, championing the career growth of early-career professionals through Individual Development Plans and on-the-job coaching.
* Serve as the firm’s local quality SME across QMS maturity, supplier quality, CAPA and deviations, audit and inspection readiness, remediation, and product development, and advise clients on evolving regulatory guidance.
* Lead delivery of multiple concurrent projects, owning scope, budget, schedule, quality, risk, and client satisfaction.
* Drive thought leadership through publications, white papers, and industry conference presentations, and contribute to firmwide quality standards and best practices.
* Maintain a personal billable utilization target of approximately 60–70% while managing team staffing and utilization to meet billable hours goals.
Develop scopes, estimates, and proposals, and expand engagements with new and existing clients through your industry network. 

**What You’ll Bring**

* A minimum of fifteen years of increasing responsibility in quality services and project management for life sciences, biotech, medical device, or other FDA regulated projects.
* A minimum of five years of people leadership experience, including hiring, coaching, and developing quality professionals.
* Proven success in a consulting or professional services environment, including meeting billable utilization goals and leading client relationships
* Experience leading quality teams across capital project handover, QMS establishment, quality audits, root cause and deviation resolution, and remediation planning.

records.title: VP, Operations
records.description:
**Building the people that build the world.**

With platforms in HVAC and Detection and Measurement, SPX Technologies builds innovative solutions that enable a safer, more efficient, sustainable world. Through our RiSE talent development framework, we Reach, Identify, Strengthen, and Engage our employees to support them in their continued development. We’re a global company of problem solvers, collaborators, and innovators, and our businesses build solutions that impact the world.

As part of HVAC Cooling, SPX Cooling Technologies is a leader in high quality industrial HVAC equipment used to cool large facilities like hospitals, data centers, and power plants. With cooling towers, fans, and refrigeration units, companies rely on brands like Marley, Recold, and SGS to provide comfort and mission critical and industrial cooling solutions.

 

**How You Will Make an Impact**

The Vice President, Operations is a key member of the business unit leadership team and is responsible for the global operations strategy and execution for a rapidly growing business scaling beyond $1.5 billion in annual revenue. This leader will have responsibility for a global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities and will ensure the operations organization has the capacity, capabilities, systems, talent, and processes required to support significant organic and inorganic growth.

The VP, Operations will establish and execute a scalable global operating model that delivers world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, working capital, and customer service. This leader will drive greater consistency and integration across manufacturing locations while ensuring the operating footprint, capital investments, supply chain capabilities, and organizational structure are positioned to support long-term growth.

A critical priority will be building an operations organization capable of operating at significantly greater scale. The VP will develop strong plant and functional leaders, create clear accountability across the operations network, institutionalize continuous improvement, and partner closely with Commercial, Engineering, Product Management, Finance, Human Resources, and Supply Chain to translate business strategy into operational execution.

**What You Can Expect in This Role**

* **Develop and execute the global operations strategy** to support the business unit's growth, financial objectives, customer commitments, and long-term strategic plan.
* **Lead the global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities**, establishing common operating expectations, performance metrics, management systems, and accountability across locations.
* **Build the operational capacity and capabilities required to support a $2B+ business**, anticipating future requirements for facilities, equipment, automation, technology, supply chain, and talent.
* **Own manufacturing footprint and capacity strategy**, including plant utilization, expansions, greenfield/start-up operations, consolidations, transfers of production, and other network optimization opportunities.
* **Drive world-class performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and Working Capital**, establishing clear performance expectations and corrective actions across the global operating organization.
* **Champion a culture of safety**, ensuring consistent leadership practices, risk identification, corrective actions, compliance, and continuous improvement across all manufacturing locations.
* **Establish a disciplined Lean operating system** utilizing standard work, daily management, Kaizen, problem solving, value-stream optimization, and other continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustained performance improvement.
* **Improve operational scalability and productivity** through automation, manufacturing technology, process redesign, labor productivity, plant layout optimization, and improved utilization of assets.
* **Lead operations planning and execution**, ensuring alignment between customer demand, production capacity, labor, materials, inventory, and capital requirements through disciplined SIOP/S&OP and scheduling processes.
* **Optimize material flow and working capital**, improving inventory turns, supplier performance, schedule adherence, throughput, and overall cash conversion.
* **Develop and execute the global capital strategy for Operations**, prioritizing investments based on growth requirements, productivity, safety, quality, capacity, automation, and return on invested capital.
* **Partner with Engineering and Commercial leadership** to improve manufacturability, new product introduction, quote-to-delivery execution, capacity planning, and responsiveness to changing customer requirements.
* **Support acquisition integration and business expansion**, establishing operating standards, identifying synergies, integrating newly acquired manufacturing operations, and accelerating performance improvement.
* **Build a high-performing global Operations leadership team**, strengthening succession depth and developing Plant Managers and functional leaders capable of leading increasingly large and complex operations.
* **Create a culture of accountability and operational excellence**, ensuring leaders use data, metrics, structured problem solving, and operating rhythms to identify issues early and deliver commitments.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor to the President and business leadership team**, bringing an operations perspective to growth strategy, investment decisions, customer commitments, acquisitions, organizational design, and long-range planning.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

* Sustained improvement in employee safety and environmental performance
* World-class product quality and reduction in customer quality issues
* 95%+ on-time delivery performance and improved schedule adherence
* Year-over-year productivity and manufacturing cost improvement
* Improved inventory turns and working capital performance
* Effective deployment and return on capital investments
* Capacity and manufacturing footprint aligned with business growth
* Successful operational integration of acquisitions and new facilities
* Strong succession depth and leadership capability across Operations
* Consistent implementation of operating systems and best practices across the global manufacturing network

**What We Are Looking For**

**Required Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive operations and manufacturing leadership experience, including significant leadership of complex, multi-site operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading a large-scale global or geographically dispersed manufacturing organization.
* Experience operating within a business of significant scale and complexity, ideally $1B+ in revenue with demonstrated experience supporting substantial growth.
* Proven ability to scale manufacturing capacity, systems, processes, and organizations during periods of rapid growth.
* Demonstrated success improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, and working capital performance across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong experience in Lean manufacturing and building sustainable continuous improvement cultures.
* Experience developing manufacturing footprint strategies including plant expansions, start-ups, consolidations, transfers, and capacity investments.
* Demonstrated success developing senior operations leaders and building strong succession pipelines.
* Experience working effectively within a matrixed, global organization and influencing across functions.
* Experience operating in both union and non-union manufacturing environments preferred.
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or manufacturing operations strongly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Enterprise-level strategic thinking combined with a strong bias for execution.
* Ability to translate aggressive business growth plans into executable operations, capacity, talent, and capital strategies.
* Strong financial and business acumen with an understanding of operating margin, manufacturing economics, capital allocation, working capital, and return on investment.
* Demonstrated ability to establish operating systems, metrics, governance, and accountability across a diverse manufacturing network.
* Strong change leadership capability and demonstrated success leading organizations through significant growth and transformation.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to operate effectively from the plant floor through the executive leadership team.
* Ability to identify emerging operational risks, resolve near-term issues, and simultaneously build the capabilities required for long-term growth.
* Strong knowledge of ERP, planning, manufacturing technology, automation, and data-driven operating environments.

**Education & Certifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
* Lean/Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement certification preferred.

**Travel & Working Environment**

* Significant domestic and international travel required to maintain strong leadership presence across the global manufacturing network.
* Regular interaction within manufacturing environments with varying levels of noise, temperature, and other plant conditions.

**How we live our culture**

Our culture is at the center of what we do and, more importantly, who we are. Our core values set a standard for how we manage ourselves, and our Leadership Model sets the standard for how we engage with each other. Whether you are an individual contributor or you lead a large team, each of us leads at SPX.

**What benefits do we offer?**

We know that the well-being of our employees is integral. Our benefits include:

* Generous and flexible paid time off including paid personal time off, caregiver, parental, and volunteer leave
* Competitive health insurance plans and 401(k) match, with benefits starting day one
* Competitive and performance-based compensation packages and bonus plans
* Educational assistance, leadership development programs, and recognition programs

**Our commitment to embrace diversity to build a culture of inclusion at SPX**

We value different backgrounds, experiences, and voices at SPX, and we are committed to challenging ourselves, openly communicating, and striving to improve every day. We believe in creating an inclusive work environment where everyone has a voice and is encouraged to realize their fullest potential.

SPX is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer committed to making selection decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis.

records.title: Vice President of Operations
records.description:
**About the Role:**

The Vice President of Operations in a manufacturing environment is responsible for overseeing and optimizing all operational aspects to ensure efficiency, quality, and profitability. This role requires strategic leadership to align operational goals with the company’s overall vision and market demands. The VP of Operations will drive continuous improvement initiatives, manage cross-functional teams, and implement best practices to enhance production processes and supply chain management. They will also play a critical role in financial planning, resource allocation, and risk management to support sustainable growth. Ultimately, this position ensures that manufacturing operations meet customer expectations while maintaining compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations.
* Proven track record of strategic planning and successful execution in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
* Demonstrated ability to lead large teams and manage cross-functional projects.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA) or relevant advanced degree.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Familiarity with advanced data analytics tools and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
* Previous experience in a senior executive role within the manufacturing industry.
* Certifications related to operations management or leadership development.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute comprehensive operational strategies that support the company’s business objectives and growth plans.
* Lead and mentor senior management and operational teams to foster a culture of high performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Oversee production planning, quality control, supply chain logistics, and maintenance to maximize operational efficiency and product quality.
* Collaborate with finance to manage budgets, forecast operational costs, and analyze financial performance to inform decision-making.
* Utilize data analytics to monitor key performance indicators, identify operational risks, and implement corrective actions promptly.
* Drive talent development initiatives to build a skilled and motivated workforce aligned with organizational goals.
* Communicate operational plans, progress, and challenges effectively to the executive leadership team and stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental regulations, and industry standards across all manufacturing sites.

**Skills:**

The required skills such as Executive Presence and Leadership are essential for inspiring and guiding diverse teams while representing the operations function at the executive level. Strategic Planning and Execution skills enable the VP to develop actionable roadmaps that align operational activities with long-term business goals. Operational Strategy expertise is applied daily to optimize manufacturing processes, improve supply chain efficiency, and ensure product quality. Communication and Presentation skills are critical for articulating complex operational plans and performance metrics to stakeholders clearly and persuasively. Delegation, Financial Planning and Analysis, Data Analysis, and Talent Development skills are utilized to empower teams, manage resources effectively, make data-driven decisions, and cultivate a high-performing workforce that drives continuous operational excellence.
