records.title: Senior Manager, Logistics Warehouse Operations
records.description:
**Position Summary**

This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship
 
 
Headquartered in Plano, TX, Samsung Electronics America (SEA) is a leader in mobile technologies, consumer electronics, home appliances, enterprise solutions and networks systems. Across each of these areas, our work drives innovation, economic growth and workforce opportunity in the United States.
 
 
For nearly five decades, Samsung has been at the forefront of technological advancements, investing over $100 billion and creating more than 20,000 jobs nationwide. Our mission? To integrate cutting-edge products, services, and AI technology to deliver smarter, sustainable, and more connected experiences that empower people to live better.
 
 
As a wholly owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., SEA offers opportunities to work alongside global visionary thinkers and innovators who are passionate about making a difference. Explore the exciting opportunities at Samsung Electronics America and discover how you can make an impact.
 
 
To learn more, visit Samsung.com. For the latest news, visit news.samsung.com/us.

**Role and Responsibilities**

**Role & Responsibilities**

At the organizational level, this role will maintain relationships across logistics, warehouse and SEA business unit employees to ensure that services are executed efficiently and timely. The role responsibilities include analyzing operations, reviewing workflows and production processes, reducing inefficiency, and ensuring that final products meet the established quality standards.

This role will actively manage all open projects to support logistics operation of SEA LPS and identify areas for continuous performance improvements. Develop and liaise with Logistics & 3PL WH staff. Generate weekly KPI and forecasting reports. Responsible for routine or standard technical problems and responds to standard requests from internal and external customers, using effective communication channels and mediums. Makes decisions within guidelines and policies, supporting goals, objectives and requirements.

**Skills and Qualifications**

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent
* Must have project management experience, PMP or equivalent preferred
* High proficiency in MS Excel, Access, PowerPoint, SQL and BI Tools
* Minimum of 3 years’ with proven experience utilizing Six Sigma and/or Lean Manufacturing initiatives in production is preferred
* Prior experience in logistics operations, supply chain management and/or warehousing, 3PL (managing relationships) preferred
* Strong analytical skills with the ability to develop and create original analysis.
* Strong interpersonal and consensus building skills
* Must have experience with SAP or similar business enterprise purchasing, inventory control and/or procurement management system required
* Must have Microsoft Office Suite of PC software applications experience with Excel spreadsheet and PowerPoint preparation skills operating in an NT LAN/WAN systems environment
* Demonstrated ability to influence others in acceptance and approval and to provide clarification
* The ability to plan, organize and prioritize multiple and simultaneous projects, issues and activities
* The ability to read, interpret and simplify complex information from various documents to create clarity and ease of understanding
* Ability to communicate in writing, through email, reports, presentations, or orally, product logistics matters to all audiences
* The ability to clearly define objectives, identify tasks and work assignments, give direction and make decisions based upon applied knowledge of alternatives and work experience
Interact with all levels within the organization and has frequent external contacts 

Work is performed both in an office setting and warehouse environment. Operate a computer keyboard and view a video display terminal between 50% - 90% of work time, including prolonged periods of time. Requires considerable (50%) work utilizing high visual acuity/detail, numeric/character distinction, and moderate hand/finger dexterity. Performs work under time schedules and stress which are normally periodic or cyclical, including time sensitive deadlines, intellectual challenge, some language barriers, and project management deadlines. Machines, tools, equipment, and work aids include printers, copiers, faxes, and other equipment commonly associated with an office work area. May require working additional hours beyond normal schedule, including weekends and or holidays. 25% Travel varies depending on position. Consistently demonstrates a commitment to policies and procedures, including but not limited to, attendance, confidentiality, conflict of interest, and ethical responsibilities.

#LI-KR1

Life @ Samsung - https://www.samsung.com/us/careers/life-at-samsung/

Benefits @ Samsung - https://www.samsung.com/us/careers/benefits/ 
 
 
 
The salary range for this role, for candidates based in California, is expected to be between $159,000 and $196,500. Actual pay will be determined considering factors such as relevant skills and experience, and comparison to other employees in the role.

 
 

Regular full-time employees (salaried or hourly) have access to benefits including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, 401(k), Employee Purchase Program, Tuition Assistance (after 12 months), Paid Time Off, Student Loan Program (after 12 months), Wellness Incentives, and many more. In addition, regular full-time employees (salaried or hourly) are eligible for MBO bonus compensation, based on company, division, and individual performance.
 
 
To ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process, please do not use GenAI tools during your interview unless explicitly permitted; failure to adhere to these guidelines may result in disqualification from the recruitment process.

\* Please visit Samsung membership to see Privacy Policy, which defaults according to your location. You can change Country/Language at the bottom of the page.

At Samsung, we believe that innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We aim to create a global team where everyone belongs and has equal opportunities, inspiring our talent to be their true selves. Together, we are building a better tomorrow for our customers, partners, and communities.

* Samsung Electronics America, Inc. and its subsidiaries are committed to employing a diverse workforce, and provide Equal Employment Opportunity for all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, status as a qualified individual with a disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

**Reasonable Accommodations for Qualified Individuals with Disabilities During the Application Process**

Samsung Electronics America is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application process. If you have a disability and require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application process, please contact our Reasonable Accommodation Team (855-557-3247) or SEA\_Accommodations\_Ext@sea.samsung.com for assistance. This number is for accommodation requests only and is not intended for general employment inquiries.

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality, Fauna
records.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Senior Manager to lead the quality, test engineering, and reliability organization supporting our robots from development through production. 
In this role, you will improve product and manufacturing quality while building the testing capabilities needed to scale. Your organization will support new product introduction through volume production across our facilities, suppliers, and manufacturing partners. 
You will build the team and its engineering leadership, set the technical direction, and establish quality standards and validation processes. You will turn changing product and manufacturing needs into a roadmap that supports higher production volumes and additional sites. 
The ideal candidate is a technically strong engineering leader who has improved quality and reliability for products where hardware and software must work together. They can evaluate test strategies and guide critical supplier, production, and reliability investigations. They grow engineers and leaders, and make clear decisions on scope and priority while product designs and manufacturing processes are changing. 
 
Key job responsibilities 

* Architect the quality, test engineering, and reliability organization. Assess capability gaps, define the staffing and investment plan, and hire and develop the engineering leaders and teams needed to scale.
* Establish supplier and factory quality teams, with Fauna engineers embedded at manufacturing sites. Strengthen and scale the quality system to support new products and increasing production volumes.
* Define and lead the reliability strategy, working with our engineers to improve robot performance and durability.
* Build and scale reliability labs and test infrastructure to support product development and production growth.
* Scale and develop the manufacturing test engineering team, shaping its structure, growing its leaders, and strengthening its capabilities to support new products and increasing production volumes.
* Deploy and qualify production test systems across our facilities and manufacturing partners. Partner with the software and systems team on automation and traceable results, and improve repeatability, cycle time, and failure diagnosis.
* Partner with engineering and operations to embed quality, reliability, and testability into product design and production readiness.
* Establish quality and reliability metrics and use production, test, and field data to guide priorities and drive sustained improvement.

 
About the team 
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
 
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
 
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
 
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
 
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you

New York, New York

Day (United States of America)

**Description:**
----------------

**Director of Operations**

Take on a highly visible leadership role at NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell Medical Center, helping shape the continued growth and evolution of a highly dynamic campus. As the Director of Operations, you will provide operational leadership for a portfolio of clinical programs and campus initiatives. You will work closely with senior, clinical and administrative leaders to advance strategic priorities, support growth, and ensure high-quality, efficient and patient-centered operations. The Director will have administrative oversight of key clinical services and play a significant role in capital and construction projects across the campus. This includes operational planning, construction coordination, logistics, moves and relocations, and the activation of new and renovated spaces.

The Director will also help plan for clinical capacity and growth, working with clinical and operational leaders to anticipate future needs and align space, resources, workflows and infrastructure to support evolving patient care and new programs. Serving as a key interdisciplinary partner across the campus, the Director will bring together physicians, nursing, clinical departments, support services, Facilities, Engineering, Design & Construction, Finance and other teams to coordinate complex initiatives and solve operational challenges.

The Director will also lead organizational readiness initiatives and support emergency preparedness and other campus priorities on behalf of senior leadership.

**Preferred Criteria**

 

* Master’s Degree in Business Administration, HealthCare Administration or related field

**Required Criteria**

 

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration or related field
* Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive responsible experience in business planning and process improvement, including five (5) years of management experience in a hospital setting
* Consistent demonstration of a commitment to quality, customer-centeredness, productivity and process improvement.
* Proven ability to direct and manage with concurrent responsibility for more than one operational area
* Demonstrate success in effectively leading a highly matrixed/cross-functional environment
* Demonstrated leadership, communication and interpersonal skills
* Knowledge of Article 28 Regulations

Join a healthcare system where employee engagement is at an all-time high. Here we foster a culture of respect, belonging, and inclusion. Enjoy comprehensive and competitive benefits that support you and your family in every aspect of life. Start your life-changing journey today.

Please note that all roles require on-site presence (variable by role). Therefore, all employees should live within a commutable distance to NYP.

NYP will not reimburse for travel expenses.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
Who is Taco Bell?

Taco Bell is a leading Mexican-inspired quick service restaurant brand that is a part of Yum! Brands, Inc. which includes Pizza Hut and KFC. Founded on innovation and passion with Glen Bell bringing tacos to the masses in a world of hot dog and hamburger stands in 1962, today we have nearly 7000 restaurants in the United States and over 400 restaurants in 27 countries outside of the United States. The future holds 2,000 more restaurants across the globe within the next decade. It's easy to see we're in the business of making tacos, but at heart, we're a business that's fueled by the Live Mas energy and passion of people serving people.

What is "Live Mas"?

Equally important to the job role and responsibilities is making sure the Director of Operations can represent the amazing Live Mas! culture that is Taco Bell. At Taco Bell, we embrace breakthrough thinking and innovative ideas that continue to differentiate us from our competitors. We have a maniacal focus on our customers, never follow, and always celebrate the accomplishments of our people. If you want to have fun serving great food to our customers, we would love to meet with you.

Job Description:

About this Job: Reporting to the General Manager, the Director of Operations is responsible for all aspects of operations including people, customers, sales and profits. This leader has up to 3 area coaches as direct reports compiling 12 restaurants. They drive excellence in day-to-day operations; hire, train, coach, & support managers; plan and set goals; focus on problem solving/process improvement; set standards; recognize and motivate area managers, unit level management & their teams. Influence people to drive business results and franchise partnership

The Day-to-Day:

Build People Capability

* Recruit and equip the best operators in the world to deliver great customer experiences
* Build a healthy and robust bench of developed and capable Managers
* Hold Area Coaches accountable for people, customer, sales and profit targets
* Lead by example be a culture champion and live by Taco Bell principles
* Leverage culture and people capability to fuel brand performance
* Resolution oriented in all Employee Relations (ER) activities; provides needed
ER assistance to managers; proactive in addressing ER needs in the market 

 

Deliver a Consistent Customer Experience

* Provides leadership for each manager in the market to ensure customer satisfaction
* Leverage customer programs to coach and improve on execution opportunities
* Train, coach and hold accountable Area Coaches and Restaurant Managers for executing the Taco Bell Operating System and delivering Brand Standards including food safety
* Identify and act with urgency to resolve Brand protection issues
* Excellent execution of Global Operating System initiatives
* Absolutely uncompromising execution of the highest standards of their local regulation around occupational safety and health standards for employee working conditions, and their company safety and security policy

Grow the Brand, Sales, and Profits

* Partners with each Manager in the market to build sales over last year's sales achievement
* Training and operations execution of marketing promotions
* Train and coach Area Coaches how to teach RGMs to use the tools and processes to improve restaurant financial results
* Coach to deliver restaurant profit targets in every restaurant
* Leads the way by working with each Area Coach in the market to deliver profit goals and meet targeted flow-thru objectives; utilizes available reports to identify opportunities; encourages a top-line orientation through operational focus; ensures that correct operational procedures are followed at all times
* Build capability to improve problem solving and planning skills through hands-on demonstrations
* Exhibits ownership working with Management to resolve chronic Repair & Maintenance issues; determines causes of excessive R&M; gathers R&M issues; identifies trends and takes to R&M Business Partners

Minimum Requirements-

Is This You?

* Bachelor's Degree preferred
* Strong Quick Service Restaurant Experience, balancing product quality with fast service times
* Is a Dynamic, energetic and positive leader, a self-starter, proactively driven to get things done and does the right thing for the business
* Exhibits unrivaled leadership behaviors; providing coaching, developing the team, driving culture, problem solving, strong communication, time management, executing tasks and achieving results through others
* 10+ years Restaurant Management experience with strong people growing record, recruiting talent, development and performance management
* Corporate restaurant company field operations leader experience
* Has lead multiple managers of multiple high volume units in an area
* Extensive Area Coach experience leading 6-8 restaurant general managers
* Has personally ran a successful restaurant and has knowledge of restaurant operations and expectations for team member's positions
* Corporate office Cross-Functional leading teams experience
* Good communication skills, and strong interpersonal and conflict resolution skills with exceptional team building capability

Why Taco Bell?

We truly believe that where you work matters, and we know a thing or two about what makes employees happy. Join us on our mission of feeding people's lives with Mas!

* We are about more than just building restaurantswe connect with our fans through their passions including sports, gaming, and music
* We know that employees want a company they can live and grow with; they crave a unique culture that fosters creativity and encourages pursuit of passion, and they look for opportunities to take risks, develop skills and learn in ways that fit their lifestyle
* We foster a culture of authenticity and believe all people can make a difference

At The Resource Group, we build strong relationships with provider teams, working alongside them to improve supply chain operations and lower non-payroll expenses, all in support of delivering quality patient care. Responsibilities for this role can be found below:

 

* Direct the development and implementation of comprehensive policies and standard operating procedures that align supply chain services with the organization's long-term productivity and strategic objectives.
* Assume ultimate accountability for the preparation and management of departmental budgets, ensuring strict compliance with allocated funding and leading all internal and external regulatory audits.
* Oversee complex supplier relationships and lead large-scale integration teams to ensure seamless operational transitions and optimized resource utilization across multiple facilities and/or large sites.
* Provide executive oversight for the continuous evaluation of supply chain processes to guarantee total adherence to accrediting bodies and national regulatory agency requirements.
* Cultivate executive-level relationships with healthcare facility leadership to enhance customer service delivery and ensure that supply chain work allocations support the highest standards of clinical quality.
* Direct team staffing initiatives and leadership development frameworks to ensure the alignment of work assignments with organizational goals, while fostering a high-performing culture.

* Required Credential(s): 
 None Required.

**Additional Preferences:**

* A Master's degree
* 8+ years of professional experience (customer relations, people management, project management, multi-site operations management)

records.description:
**Company Description**

A best-in-class city that attracts best-in-class talent, Philadelphia is an incredible place to build a career. From our thriving arts scene and rich history to our culture of passion and grit, there are countless reasons to love living and working here. With a workforce of over 30,000 people, and more than 1,000 different job categories, the City of Philadelphia offers boundless opportunities to make an impact.

As an employer, the City of Philadelphia values inclusion, integrity, innovation, empowerment, and hard work above all else. We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

***What we offer***

* **Impact** - The work you do here matters to millions.
* **Growth** - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
* **Diversity & Inclusion** - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
* **Benefits** - We care about your well-being.

***Agency Description***

The mission of the Department of Revenue is to collect tax and non-tax revenue due to the City and tax revenue due to the School District of Philadelphia while providing service to customers that is fair and efficient and ensuring that the City provides services that the residents can see, touch, and feel. The Department’s revenue collections enable the Administration to invest in the Mayor’s strategic priorities, including housing, education, and making Philadelphia the safest, cleanest, and greenest big city in the nation with economic opportunity for everyone.

***Work-Life***

Working hours are generally 37.5 hours per week. Our team is full-time on office days.

 **Job Description**

The Continuous Improvement Director leads the Continuous Improvement pillar within the Revenue Strategic Transformation division. This role identifies, prioritizes, and delivers process improvement initiatives that increase operational efficiency, reduce waste, and improve the experience of both employees and the residents and businesses the department serves.

The CI Director brings a disciplined improvement practice to a large public organization: mapping how work actually flows, finding where it breaks down, and redesigning it in partnership with the units that own it. Success depends on facilitation, analytical rigor, and the ability to see how decisions in one part of the department create consequences in another.

The CI Director owns the improvement methodology, process mapping and redesign discipline, customer satisfaction measurement, documentation standards, and the training that builds continuous improvement capability across the department. The role leads a small team and is expected to develop that team, not simply directing its work.

The CI Director works in close partnership with the Executive Director, who provides strategic direction, and coordinates with the division's other pillars: Operations, Project Management, Change Management, and Innovation and Advanced Analytics.

***Essential Functions***

Continuous Improvement of Methodology and Execution

* Design and maintain the department's continuous improvement framework, applying Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, root cause analysis, and process redesign methods as appropriate to each initiative.
* Lead current-state process mapping across business units, documenting workflows, identifying waste, rework, and handoff failures, and designing future-state processes in partnership with the relevant unit.
* Lead improvement initiatives from intake through implementation, ensuring changes are measurable, sustainable, and owned by the business unit responsible for execution.
* Design and maintain controls and monitoring mechanisms so improvements are sustained and do not revert to prior practice.
* Apply design thinking to identify where a local improvement would create downstream burden elsewhere, and design accordingly.

2. Intake and Prioritization

* Capture improvement opportunities from business unit requests, performance data, customer feedback, staff suggestions, and strategic priorities.
* Apply a structured prioritization framework covering feasibility screening, scoring, and portfolio balancing to select initiatives that deliver the highest value relative to effort and risk.
* Operate the shared intake and routing protocol with the Project Management Office and the Innovation and Advanced Analytics unit, so that improvement requests, project requests, and pilot concepts follow one clear path.
* Maintain a portfolio tracker providing visibility into active, pipeline, and completed initiatives with documented outcomes.

3. Customer Satisfaction Measurement

* Own design, distribution, and analysis of customer satisfaction surveys, including the external survey of residents and businesses and the internal business unit survey.
* Produce and distribute monthly reports with trend analysis and actionable insight.
* Route improvement opportunities identified through customer feedback into the intake process.
* Coordinate with Communications on distribution and messaging, and with Innovation and Advanced Analytics on data integration and reporting.

4. Standards, Procedures, and Process Documentation

* Establish departmental standards for processing documentation so procedures, workflows, and operational guides are created and maintained consistently across units.
* Provide templates, frameworks, and guidance to business units documenting their own processes, with Continuous Improvement serving as the quality standard-setter.
* Maintain a central repository of documented processes accessible to leadership and business units.

5. Training, Culture, and Team Development

* Develop and deliver a continuous improvement education plan tailored to three audiences: executive leadership for strategic awareness, managers and supervisors for application skills, and frontline staff for mindset and participation.
* Integrate a continuous improvement introduction into departmental onboarding in partnership with Human Resources.
* Identify and develop improvement champions within business units who sustain the practice beyond individual initiatives.
* Directly develop the Continuous Improvement Specialist and Project Coordinator, building their capability in process mapping, intake discipline, and initiative support.

6. Reporting and Impact Measurement

* Track and report measurable outcomes for each initiative: time saved, errors reduced, cost avoided, satisfaction improved, or other relevant metrics.
* Produce quarterly impact reports for the Executive Director documenting portfolio progress, results achieved, and lessons learned.
* Use outcome data to support the case for continued investment in staffing, tools, and initiative scope.

***Competencies, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

* Proven leadership in strategic planning, organizational development, and change management.
* Expertise in Lean Six Sigma, process mapping, and performance benchmarking.
* Strong ability to lead cross-functional teams and foster collaboration.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
* Advanced analytical and data-driven decision-making capabilities.

 **Qualifications**

***Required***

* Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in continuous improvement, process improvement, or operational excellence.
* Lean Six Sigma certification at Green Belt or higher, or equivalent recognized process improvement certification.
* Demonstrated command of improvement methodologies and the judgment to select the right approach for a given problem.
* Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from intake through measurable results.
* The ability to see how processes connect across an organization and how a change in one area affects others.
* Strong facilitation, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Experience supervising, mentoring, or developing staff.

***Preferred***

* Master's degree in a related field.
* Experience in government, public sector, or nonprofit organizations.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent advanced certification.
* Change management certification such as Prosci.
* Project management certification such as PMP.
* Experience designing and analyzing customer satisfaction surveys and Net Promoter Score programs.
* Experience building an improvement function where none previously existed.

 **Additional Information**

**TO APPLY:** **Interested candidates must submit a resume.**

Salary Range: $90,500 - $115,000

**Discover the Perks of Being a City of Philadelphia Employee:**

* **Transportation**: City employees get unlimited **FREE** public transportation all year long through SEPTA’s Key Advantage program. Employees can ride on SEPTA buses, subways, trolleys, and regional rail for their daily commute and more.
* Parental Benefits: The City offers its employees 8 weeks of paid parental leave.
* We offer Comprehensive health coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.
* Our wellness program offers eligibility into the discounted medical plan
* Employees receive paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays
* Generous retirement savings options are available
* **Pay off your student loans faster** - As a qualifying employer, City of Philadelphia employees are eligible to participate in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Join the ranks of hundreds of employees who have already benefited from this program and achieved student loan forgiveness.
* **Unlock Tuition Discounts and Scholarships** - The City of Philadelphia has forged partnerships with over a dozen esteemed colleges and universities in the area, ensuring that our employees have access to a wide range of tuition discounts and scholarships. Experience savings of 10% to 40% on your educational expenses, extending not only to City employees but in some cases, spouse and dependents too!

Join the City of Philadelphia team today and seize these incredible benefits designed to enhance your financial well-being and personal growth!

* ***The successful candidate must be a city of Philadelphia resident within six months of hire***

Effective May 22, 2023, vaccinations are **no longer required** for new employees that work in non-medical, non-emergency or patient facing positions with the City of Philadelphia. As a result, only employees in positions providing services that are patient-facing medical care (ex: Nurses, doctors, emergency medical personnel), must be fully vaccinated.

The City of Philadelphia is an Equal Opportunity employer and does not permit discrimination based on race, ethnicity, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, marital status, source of income, familial status, genetic information or domestic or sexual violence victim status. If you believe you were discriminated against, call the Philadelphia Commission on Human Relations at 215-686-4670 or send an email to faqpchr@phila.gov.

For more information, go to: Human Relations Website: http://www.phila.gov/humanrelations/Pages/default.aspx

records.description:
**Company Description**

Domino’s Pizza, which began in 1960 as a single store location in Ypsilanti, MI, has had a lot to celebrate lately: we’re a reshaped, reenergized brand of honesty, transparency and accountability – not to mention, great food! In the rise to becoming a true technology leader, the brand is now consistently one of the top five companies in online transactions and 65% of our sales in the U.S. are taken through digital channels. The brand continues to ‘deliver the dream’ to local business owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores. That’s just the tip of the iceberg…or as we might say, one “slice” of the pie! If this sounds like a brand you’d like to be a part of, consider joining our team!

 **Job Description**

The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.

Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.

**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**

In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:

Be Curious

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

 
**Additional Information**

Benefits: 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

records.title: Director of Medical Group Operations
records.description:
Overview:

Director of Medical Group Operations| Medical Practice Leadership

Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group| Aurora, Illinois

Full-Time | Exempt | Days 
Starting Annual Salary: $101,212.80 – $146,619.20

Lead Practice Excellence. Empower Providers. Advance Patient Access.

Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group, a member of Prime Healthcare, is seeking an experienced and collaborative Director of Medical Group Operations to lead the operational performance, growth, and success of physician practices and ambulatory clinics throughout the Aurora market.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a healthcare operations leader who enjoys partnering with physicians, practice leaders, and executive leadership to strengthen practice performance, improve patient access, optimize workflows, and advance strategic growth across a multi-specialty medical group.

We are looking for someone who can think strategically, lead confidently, and drive operational excellence while supporting providers in delivering exceptional, patient-centered care throughout the community.

About Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group

Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group brings together primary care and specialty providers across Illinois, with medical group locations affiliated with Prime Healthcare's Illinois hospitals, including Mercy Medical Center in Aurora.

Our physicians, advanced practice providers, practice leaders, and support teams work collaboratively to provide accessible, coordinated, high-quality care while creating an exceptional patient experience.

As part of Prime Healthcare, Illinois Medical Group benefits from the resources, support, and stability of a nationally recognized health system while maintaining a strong commitment to the healthcare needs of the communities it serves.

Responsibilities:

As Director of Medical Group Operations, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for physician practices and ambulatory services while supporting growth, operational efficiency, provider engagement, and exceptional patient experiences.

* Lead day-to-day operations of physician practices and medical group clinics to ensure high-quality patient care and operational excellence.
* Partner with physicians, practice managers, and executive leadership to develop strategies that support growth, patient access, and performance improvement.
* Oversee staffing, budgeting, productivity, scheduling, and resource allocation across multiple practice locations.
* Monitor operational, financial, quality, and patient experience metrics while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with organizational policies, regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and professional practice guidelines.
* Drive initiatives focused on patient access, provider satisfaction, workflow optimization, revenue enhancement, and service-line development.
* Develop, mentor, and support practice leaders and staff while creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, and exceptional service.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree in business or healthcare management is preferred.
* Master’s degree in business or healthcare management preferred.
* Minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in medical practice management required (with direct experience managing the revenue cycle).
* Knowledge of Accounts Receivable management, coding, Medicare & Medicaid regulations, payor contracting, and Billing & Collections.
* Knowledge of credentialing, regulatory compliance, etc.
* Frequent local travel time required.

The Leader Who Will Thrive Here

You are a collaborative, results-driven healthcare leader who is passionate about medical practice operations, provider engagement, and patient access. You thrive in a fast-paced, multi-site environment where relationship-building, operational excellence, and strategic leadership are essential.

You understand that successful medical group leadership goes beyond managing day-to-day operations. It requires vision, accountability, and the ability to bring physicians, practice leaders, and staff together around shared goals that improve access, efficiency, patient satisfaction, and overall performance.

You are a self-starter and hands-on leader who communicates openly, follows through, takes accountability, and is comfortable stepping in to solve operational challenges. You enjoy developing teams, improving workflows, and partnering closely with providers and executive leadership to strengthen medical group performance. These qualities align with the leadership profile established for the Aurora opening.

Why Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group?

At Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group, you'll have the opportunity to lead and develop a network of physician practices while partnering closely with providers, practice leaders, and healthcare executives to strengthen outpatient operations and improve the patient experience.

You'll have the opportunity to improve patient access, strengthen revenue cycle and operational performance, support provider success, develop practice leaders, and help drive the continued growth of a multi-specialty medical group.

Prime Healthcare's Illinois Medical Group network serves communities through medical groups affiliated with hospitals across the state, including Mercy Medical Center, Resurrection Medical Center, Saint Francis Hospital, Saint Joseph Hospital, Saint Joseph Medical Center, Saint Mary of Nazareth Hospital, St. Mary’s Hospital, and Olympia Fields Hospital. As part of Prime Healthcare, the Medical Group benefits from the resources of Prime Healthcare, stability, and opportunities of a nationally recognized, award-winning health system.

If you're ready to bring your medical group leadership experience to an organization where you can make a measurable impact on practice performance, provider engagement, patient access, and patient care, we encourage you to apply.

#LI-JJ3

#LI-TA1

Pay Transparency:

Prime Healthcare Illinois Medical Group offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package that provides employees the flexibility to tailor benefits according to their individual needs. Our Total Rewards package includes, but is not limited to, paid time off, a 401K retirement plan, medical, dental, and vision coverage, tuition reimbursement, and many more voluntary benefit options. A reasonable compensation estimate for this role, which includes estimated wages, benefits, and other forms of compensation, is $101,212.80 to $146,619.20 on an annualized basis. The exact starting compensation to be offered will be determined at the time of selecting an applicant for hire, in which a wide range of factors will be considered, including but not limited to, skillset, years of applicable experience, education, credentials and licensure.

The company is dedicated to empowering its staff with a comprehensive, competitive benefits package, allowing them the freedom to customize their benefits to fit their unique needs. Our abundant resources, programs, and voluntary options serve as a foundation for individual growth and well-being. Learn more here: https://www.primehealthcare.com/benefitsthatmattermost/

Employment Status: Full Time Shift: Days Equal Employment Opportunity:

Company is an equal employment opportunity employer. Company prohibits discrimination against any applicant or employee based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, age (subject to applicable law), disability, military status, genetic information or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. The Company also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories. records.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

postedPay.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

records.description:
Department Overview:

The Department of Medicine (DoM) at OHSU is comprised of a diverse community of faculty, staff, clinicians, researchers, educators, and learners dedicated to advancing patient care, education, and research across ten divisions.

The Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, quality management, and performance improvement support for inpatient clinical services across the Department of Medicine's ten specialty divisions and care sites. Reporting to the Vice Chair of Clinical Practice and partnering closely with the Vice Chair for Administration, this position serves as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and clinical effectiveness initiatives.

Function/Duties of Position:

Working collaboratively with DoM and OHSU Health quality leaders, division leadership, hospital operations, finance, revenue cycle, informatics, care management, nursing leadership, clinical documentation teams, and physician leaders, the Director advances the Department's inpatient quality, operational, clinical, and financial goals through the design, implementation, and oversight of standardized processes, performance improvement efforts, operational reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Emphasis is placed on quality programing and outcomes, patient safety, clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, revenue cycle performance, operational efficiency, provider productivity, inpatient capacity management, and growth planning across all Department of Medicine inpatient services. The Director supports a broad portfolio of inpatient programs spanning multiple clinical specialties and care settings.

This position functions within a highly matrixed environment and serves as a key liaison between departmental leadership and enterprise partners, ensuring alignment with OHSU Health strategic priorities, quality objectives, and high-reliability organizational principles.

**Inpatient Quality and Operations Leadership and Oversight**

* Work in direct partnership with the DoM Vice Chair of Clinical Practice, DoM Associate Vice Chair of Inpatient Services, Healthcare quality leaders, and other institutional leaders to oversee and coordinate quality-focused inpatient care across Department of Medicine divisions.
* Provide strategic administrative leadership and operational oversight for Department of Medicine inpatient programs and services.
* Serve as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Partner with division heads, section heads, medical directors, healthcare administrators, quality leaders, and physician leaders to identify and address operational and quality barriers affecting patient safety, access, efficiency, provider experience, and clinical outcomes.
* Shape and implement standardized inpatient quality, safety, and operational best practices across medicine specialties.
* Coordinate departmental quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing medical errors, serious safety events, healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired conditions, avoidable readmissions, preventable complications, and patient harm.
* Lead administrative efforts related to inpatient quality programs, patient safety activities, inpatient capacity management, patient flow, consult services, discharge efficiency, care coordination, and service-line optimization.
* Support departmental participation in mortality reviews, safety event reviews, quality committees, accreditation activities, regulatory preparedness efforts, and institutional quality initiatives.
* Establish and maintain departmental quality and operational governance structures, including scorecards, dashboards, performance reviews, and accountability processes.
* Partner with healthcare quality teams to identify opportunities for improvement and coordinate development of corrective action plans.
* Serve as the primary administrative liaison between Department of Medicine leadership, inpatient programs, Healthcare quality teams, and hospital operations leadership.
* Monitor operational, quality, and patient safety performance measures and drive action planning to improve outcomes.
* Facilitate multidisciplinary teams and stakeholder groups responsible for advancing inpatient quality, safety, throughput, and operational effectiveness.

**Revenue Cycle, Billing, Coding, and Clinical Documentation Integrity**

* Serve as the Department's operational lead for inpatient professional revenue cycle performance.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Professional Coding, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Finance, Compliance, and physician leaders to improve revenue capture, reimbursement, and operational performance.
* Evaluate and improve inpatient provider documentation practices, coding accuracy, charge capture processes, and billing workflows.
* Lead provider education efforts related to documentation requirements, coding regulations, payer expectations, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance standards.
* Monitor inpatient professional fee performance, wRVU generation, Case Mix Index (CMI), coding trends, denials, reimbursement outcomes, and documentation quality measures.
* Develop dashboards and performance reporting tools that support transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify specialty-specific opportunities for revenue optimization, operational efficiency, and documentation improvement.

**Performance Improvement and Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead complex inpatient operational and quality improvement initiatives utilizing Lean, process improvement, project management, and change management methodologies.
* Design and implement department-wide initiatives focused on improving quality outcomes, patient safety, throughput, provider experience, financial performance, and operational consistency.
* Conduct workflow analyses and redesign efforts to eliminate inefficiencies, reduce variation in care delivery, and improve service performance.
* Collaborate with Quality, Analytics, Finance, Informatics, and Operations teams to establish measurable goals and monitor outcomes.
* Develop project charters, implementation plans, success metrics, and performance benchmarks for strategic initiatives.
* Support departmental strategic planning activities and implementation of enterprise priorities related to inpatient growth, quality, and operational excellence.
* Advance high-reliability organization principles and support compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements.

**Data Analytics, Reporting, and Financial Performance**

* Develop and maintain operational, financial, quality, patient safety, and utilization reporting structures for departmental and divisional leadership.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive inpatient quality scorecards and dashboards.
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators including:
 + Analyze trends in inpatient volumes, utilization, consult activity, throughput, revenue cycle performance, patient outcomes, and quality metrics.
 + Translate complex operational and quality data into actionable recommendations for leaders.
 + Benchmark Department performance against institutional, regional, and national metrics when available.
 + Support financial forecasting, business case development, and investment planning for inpatient growth initiatives.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Committee Leadership**

* Represent the Department of Medicine on institutional committees related to quality, patient safety, inpatient operations, revenue cycle, clinical documentation, care management, patient flow, and performance improvement.
* Build collaborative partnerships with hospital administrators, nursing leaders, physicians, quality teams, informatics, finance, and operational stakeholders.
* Provide subject matter expertise regarding inpatient quality, safety, operational performance, workflow redesign, and professional revenue optimization.
* Lead communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management activities for major inpatient initiatives.
* Support development of a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, patient safety, and operational excellence throughout Department of Medicine inpatient programs.

Required Qualifications:

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field is required. Master’s degree may substitute for one (1) year of experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in clinical operations or healthcare administration, with at least two (2) years in a formal leadership role.
* Experience supporting inpatient hospital operations, quality improvement, patient safety, healthcare finance, revenue cycle, or operational excellence initiatives.
* Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives within healthcare organizations.
* Experience working collaboratively with physician leaders, nursing leadership, and hospital operational teams.
* Experience developing performance metrics, scorecards, dashboards, and operational improvement plans.

**Competencies**

* Strong knowledge of inpatient healthcare operations and physician practice management.
* Strong knowledge of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability organizational principles.
* Knowledge of inpatient reimbursement methodologies, documentation requirements, clinical coding, and revenue cycle practices.
* Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and quality reporting requirements affecting inpatient healthcare delivery.
* Advanced analytical, reporting, and data interpretation skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop quality scorecards, operational dashboards, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Ability to analyze complex clinical, operational, financial, and quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operational and performance improvement initiatives across multiple clinical specialties.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary efforts focused on reducing medical errors, improving patient outcomes, and advancing a culture of safety.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, Epic, reporting platforms, and healthcare analytics tools.
* Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business case development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications:

**Education**

Master’s Degree in Health Care Administration, Business, Public Health or Nursing; or Bachelor’s degree with equivalent combination of education, experience and training.

**Experience**

* Eight or more years of progressively responsible healthcare operations, quality, or performance improvement experience.
* Academic medical center experience.
* Experience with inpatient physician billing and professional fee revenue cycle.
* Experience with quality reporting, patient safety programs, accreditation activities, and regulatory readiness.
* Experience with Epic reporting, provider productivity analysis, CDI initiatives, and coding optimization.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement certification or training.
* Matrix leadership experience.

**Competencies**

Demonstrated ability to leverage advanced analytics, financial modeling, forecasting tools, artificial intelligence-enabled technologies, and other data-driven methodologies to improve operational efficiency, inform strategic decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable program growth.

Additional Details:

Professional office environment; may include occasional travel to affiliate and partner sites. In-person work schedule expected, with limited telework acceptable.

Operates in an environment with frequent interruptions, multiple competing priorities, and extensive interaction with faculty, staff, trainees, and institutional partners.

Physical location: Marquam Hill (primary)

Why apply to OHSU?: **We are Oregon's only public academic health center.** In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. **All are welcome.** OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply. To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

records.title: Director, Terminal Operations
records.description:
Overview:

**Who We Are:**

Crowley is a privately held, U.S.-owned and operated company serving the maritime, logistics and energy industries with scale in 36 nations and island territories. Our Purpose is to bravely advance what’s possible to elevate people and planet, guided by our values of Integrity, Sustainability and Drive.

With more than $3 billion in annual revenue, our solutions provide integrated supply chains with a commitment to safety and reliability in our ocean and land transportation services and facilities.

We set high standards, operate with discipline, and continuously improve how we work. Performance, operational excellence and innovation drive how we compete, grow and deliver to our customers and partners.

**Work Arrangement:**

Onsite

**What You'll Do:**

Responsible for directing the port and/or terminal operations by ensuring the company is compliant with all regulatory regulations; in addition to the safe discharge, organization, storage and movement of cargo throughout the terminal.

Responsibilities:

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Ensure all operations are in compliance with all local and federal entities and environmentally sound practices are communicated and followed.
* Responsible for interaction with vessel operations, other terminals, scheduling, damage prevention, quality, and safety initiatives.
* Establishes operating budget and reviews operating results to ensure budgeted goals are achieved.
* Ensures all accounting issues, contracting agreements and financial reporting is timely completed, managed, and administered.
* Develop mentor and manage cross functional teams and work with strategic leaders.
* Ensure all operations are in compliance with all Local and Federal Entities (OSHA, PROSHA, EPA, EQB, USCG, DOT, etc.) and all Crowley policies and procedures including ISO.
* Coordinate and negotiate outside contractor and service provider alliances/ agreements, operate in various locations, and interface/coordinate with various internal departments and external organizations.
* Responsible to oversee and participate in hiring, training, evaluation, and discipline of personnel.
* Responsible for an annual budget in excess of 30M, including investigations, and details of variances.
* Responsible for the review, verification, and approval of all major expenses related to Terminal and Port Operations in accordance to company guidelines.

Qualifications:

**Experience:**

* 8+ years prior experience preferably working in the terminal and/or stevedoring operations.
* In addition to 3 – 5 years’ experience in a supervisory experience managing cross function teams.

**Education and Credentials:**

* Bachelor's degree in logistics, business administration, transportation or related field; or a combination of post-high school and equal experience may be substituted for education.

**Technical Skills:**

* Proficient in Microsoft Office products, including Excel, Outlook and Word.
* Proficient in various terminal systems, i.e. TOS, CICS, etc.

**Other:**

* Subject to a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check to obtain your driving history.

**Competencies:**

Ability to communicate effectively verbally and in writing, including conveying technical information to technical and non-technical users. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal/external business partners. Ability to evaluate process effectiveness and develop change or alternatives. Ability to function effectively with, or as part of a team. Ability to indirectly mentor, coach, train and/or supervise employees. Ability effectively manage projects that may vary in nature and scope. Ability to utilize problem solving skills. Ability to identify complex problems and review related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions. Ability to prioritize, organize and perform multiple work assignments simultaneously. Ability to apply skill sets and demonstrate proven experience developing, improving and streamlining processes to meet established goals and objectives. Ability to manage employee and client relationships to achieve specific goals for generating and maintaining sales of products and services.

**Working Conditions:**

Works both inside an office environment and also outside in conditions of both high and low temperatures. May be exposed to odors, dust, dirt, mechanical hazards, high noise levels and potentially dangerous equipment. Must be able to crouch and stoop to get into areas with restricted headroom and be able to climb ladders. May require extended use of computer keyboard and viewing of computer monitor and ability to sit for long periods of time.

**What We Offer?**

**We inspire top talent by offering a comprehensive and competitive package that supports the diverse needs of our people—on land, at sea, in offices, and remotely.**

**Our Total Rewards include:**

 

* Competitive pay with recognition programs
* Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, and vision insurance, life and disability coverage, and paid vacation and holidays
* Leave and family support: parental leave and sick leave
* Learning and growth: access to training and development for continuous skill development
* Well-being resources: Employee Assistance Program, wellness program, and gym membership discounts

**At Crowley, we invest in you—your success, your health, and your future.**

records.title: Director of Strategy & Operations, Academic Innovation
records.description:
**Job Description**
===================

**The Opportunity**

The Director of Academic Innovation Strategy & Operations advances the Division of Academic Innovation’s strategic and operational priorities by leading complex projects, driving strategic planning and execution, overseeing professional development and events, and cultivating internal and external partnerships. This position translates divisional strategy into measurable outcomes that support academic innovation.

The successful candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership, guide cross-functional initiatives, develop team capabilities, and partner with executive leadership to advance divisional goals. This role also oversees project management, operational improvements, performance evaluation, and the development and implementation of emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools that support divisional operations.

**About us**

For over 100 years, Embry-Riddle has been the world's leading aviation and aerospace university, educating more than 30,000 students across residential campuses in Daytona Beach, Florida, and Prescott, Arizona, as well as through a global network of Worldwide locations and online programs. With more than 165,000 alumni around the world, our impact reaches every corner of the aerospace, aviation, defense and technology industries.

Today, our faculty, researchers and professional staff are advancing innovation across aviation, space, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, autonomous systems and next-generation engineering. Working alongside industry leaders, government agencies and innovators, they are solving real-world challenges and shaping the technologies that will define tomorrow.

Whether you are an educator, researcher, administrator, technologist or industry professional, your work at Embry-Riddle will contribute to something bigger than a job. Join a community driven by discovery, purpose and excellence—and help shape the future of aerospace.

* ***Generous Time Off:*** *Enjoy up to 18 days of paid leave in your first year, including 3 days granted upon hire and 15 days accrued throughout the year. You'll also receive 9+ paid holidays, including the day after Thanksgiving and the week between Christmas Eve and New Year's Day.*
* ***Tuition Coverage:*** *Get 100% tuition coverage for yourself for one undergraduate and one graduate degree, and discounted rates for your spouse and dependent children up to age 26.*
* ***Retirement Contributions:*** *ERAU contributes 6% of your base salary to your retirement plan and offers a 4% matching contribution – with no vesting period.*
* ***Personal Leave:*** *Relax with 15 days of personal leave for non-exempt employees or 18 days for exempt full-time employees in your first year.*

**Qualifications**
==================

* Master's degree in a relevant field or 2–3 years of relevant professional experience.
* Demonstrated experience in strategic planning and developing operational strategies aligned with institutional goals.
* Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects and initiatives involving diverse stakeholders.
* Experience with project management methodologies and tools; familiarity with Wrike preferred.
* Strong organizational, leadership, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
* Ability to understand stakeholder needs, communicate solutions effectively, and present confidently to audiences at all organizational levels.
* Demonstrated experience in team leadership, mentorship, and stakeholder engagement.
* Familiarity with educational technologies such as Canvas LMS; AI-enabled tools such as ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot; innovation and problem-solving methodologies such as Design Thinking; and strategic planning software such as Anthology.
* Ability to adapt to changing technologies, timelines, and departmental needs.
* Experience with event planning preferred.

To submit your application for this opportunity, please visit the Embry-Riddle Career Site and search for requisition number **R312466**. Please attach all relevant materials to your application when you apply online. Complete submissions include:

* Cover letter
* Resume
* Contact information for at least three professional references (please note that references may be contacted as part of the interview/screening process)

**Current Embry-Riddle employees:** Please apply directly through the ERAU Employee Hub Central application within Workday.

Embry-Riddle is committed to fostering a workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. We strive to ensure that all faculty, staff, and students are treated fairly and provided equal opportunities for employment, advancement, compensation, training, and other benefits of employment. Embry-Riddle makes employment decisions — including hiring, promotions, compensation, and other terms of employment — based on individual merit, qualifications, and abilities. Embry-Riddle is strongly opposed to discrimination and harassment, and such behavior is prohibited by university policy. Embry-Riddle does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, veteran status, predisposing genetic characteristics, age, religion, or pregnancy status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law, in its employment, educational programs, admissions policies, financial aid, or other school-administered programs or activities. For further information, please visit our website.

Embry-Riddle does not accept unsolicited assistance from staffing or recruitment agencies. Agencies interested in partnering with the University should contact eraujobs@erau.edu and should not contact hiring managers or other University employees directly.

To preserve the integrity and authenticity of our hiring process, candidates are expected to participate without AI-assisted coaching, real-time response generation, or recording during interviews or assessments. Embry-Riddle does not use AI to automatically screen, rank, or select candidates.
