records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**Position summary**

The Director of Operations builds and leads the infrastructure that allows Fathers, Families, & Healthy Communities (FFHC) to deliver its programs and services with excellence while growing sustainably. As a member of the leadership team, the Director of Operations oversees all operational functions: human resources, facilities, information technology and systems, and marketing and communications. The role also works closely with finance and program through a dotted-line relationship.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building and establishing structure. FFHC is at an inflection point: growing its team, strengthening its systems, and preparing for a future office and community space expansion. The Director of Operations will turn that growth into disciplined structure by establishing the policies, procedures, tools and accountability systems that set FFHC apart and free leadership and program staff to focus on the mission.

**Key responsibilities:**

**Operational Leadership & Infrastructure (25%)**

* Serve as a member of the leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, annual planning, budgeting, and decision-making.
* Lead operational priorities in FFHC's strategic plan and track progress against organizational infrastructure goals and KPIs.
* Design, document, and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) and workflows across all operational functions, with clear owners and accountability.
* With the Executive Director, build organizational structure and capacity plans that support growth, including role definitions and projected staffing for future years.
* Develop and maintain an organizational risk management and crisis response plan.
* Monitor and oversee organizational insurance policies.
* Support and oversee organizational RFP processes when needed for vendors (audit, managed, IT, insurance, etc.)
* Prepare operations reports and dashboards for the Executive Director and Board of Directors.

**Human Resources & Culture (25%)**

* Oversee all HR functions, including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, offboarding, benefits administration, payroll coordination and personnel records, in partnership with FFHC's PEO (Justworks).
* Ensure compliance with federal, state and local employment laws, including the classification of W-2 employees and contractors.
* Develop and maintain the employee handbook, HR policies, job descriptions and compensation structure.
* Lead the performance management process, including goal setting, quarterly check-ins and annual reviews.
* Develop staff professional development, leadership training, and succession plans that build institutional knowledge.
* Promote a healthy, accountable organizational culture, including staff engagement, wellness and burnout prevention.
* Oversee the intern program's administrative structure, including liaising with universities for contracting, agreements, and onboarding.

**Finance & Administration, dotted line to Finance (10%)**

* Partner with finance leadership on the annual budget, quarterly financial reporting, cash flow planning and audit preparation.
* Manage operational budgets for facilities, technology, HR, and marketing.
* Ensure financial controls and procedures are followed, including purchasing, expense reimbursement, and operational vendor payments.
* Support grant budgets, financial compliance, and reporting requirements in coordination with finance and development staff.
* Help manage banking relationships, including a line of credit, insurance coverage, and organizational contracts.

**Information Technology & Systems (15%)**

* Serve as the main point of contact for FFHC’s managed IT service provider, working closely with the main vendor representative.
* Oversee FFHC's organization-wide technology systems, including Salesforce, SharePoint and Microsoft 365, and other organizational platforms.
* Lead data governance, security, privacy and access-control procedures to protect participant and organizational information.
* Manage IT vendors and contractors, hardware and software inventory, licensing and user accounts in partnership with the managed IT service provider.
* In partnership with the managed IT service provider, develop staff technology training and ensure systems are used consistently across teams.
* Identify opportunities to automate workflows and improve efficiency.

**Facilities (10%)**

* Oversee FFHC's office and program spaces, including leases, maintenance, safety, security and vendor relationships.
* Lead planning and project management for FFHC's future office and community gathering space, including site selection, build-out and move logistics.
* Ensure workplaces meet health, safety and accessibility requirements.

**Marketing & Communications (15%)**

* Oversee FFHC's marketing and communications strategy, brand standards and messaging, in partnership with the Executive Director.
* Manage the website, social media, newsletters and outreach materials, directly or through staff, contractors and agencies.
* Lead production of FFHC's annual Impact Report and other organizational publications.
* Coordinate communications that support fundraising, program recruitment, events and community engagement.

**Supervisory responsibilities**

* Supervises operations staff, contractors and vendors across HR, IT, facilities and marketing.
* Works closely with the Director of Programs and finance leadership to align operational support with program and financial needs.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications**

* 7–10 years of progressive experience in nonprofit operations, administration or management, including at least 3 years in a leadership or supervisory role.
* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business administration or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience building operational infrastructure in a growing organization: policies, SOPs, systems and accountability structures.
* Strong working knowledge of HR practices and employment law, including hiring, performance management, benefits and compliance.
* Experience overseeing technology systems and vendors, including a PEO platform Experience managing facilities, leases or office operations.
* Experience overseeing marketing or communications work, directly or through contractors.
* Availability for some evening and weekend organizational and program events.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business administration or a related field.
* HR certification (SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP or PHR).
* Experience managing budgets and partnering with finance on budgeting, reporting and audits.
* Experience with Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, Microsoft 365 administration or a PEO such as Justworks.
* Experience leading an office relocation or facility build-out.
* Experience in an organization with a $1M–$5M budget during a period of growth.
* Experience with risk management, crisis planning or organizational compliance.
* Familiarity with workforce development, violence prevention, fatherhood or family-serving programs.
* Lived experience in, or strong ties to, the communities we serve.

**What it takes to succeed**

* **Builder's mindset:** you see an organization's potential and create the systems and structures to reach it.
* **Strategic and hands-on:** you can shape long-term plans in a leadership meeting and fix an immediate problem the same afternoon.
* **Operational excellence:** you hold yourself and others to high standards of discipline, consistency and follow-through.
* **Systems thinking:** when a problem repeats, you build a process so it doesn't happen again.
* **Attention to detail:** you catch errors in policies, budgets, contracts and data before they become problems.
* **People leadership:** you develop staff, give clear and honest feedback, and build a culture where people do their best work.
* **Sound judgment and discretion:** you handle confidential personnel, financial and participant information with care.
* **Clear communication:** you explain policies and decisions clearly to staff, leadership, the board and partners.
* **Calm under pressure:** you stay steady during transitions, crises and competing priorities.
* **Collaboration:** you build strong partnerships with program, development, finance and leadership colleagues.
* **Empathy and cultural humility:** you understand the community context of our work and lead with respect.
* **Accountability:** you own outcomes, flag problems early and keep your commitments.

**Physical requirements and work environment**

* Primarily office-based, with regular travel to program sites, partner locations and potential facility sites in Chicago.
* Ability to lift and carry supplies and equipment up to 25 pounds.
* Some evening and weekend hours for organizational and program events; schedule flexibility is offered in return.

Pay: From $85,000.00 per year

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Education:

* Master's (Preferred)

Experience:

* Operations: 3 years (Preferred)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Chicago, IL 60616

records.title: Director, Loyalty Strategy & Operations
records.description:
At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.

 

Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere.

**Introduction to the role**
----------------------------

 

The Director of Loyalty Strategy & Operations will own Brand Expedia's loyalty strategy and operational delivery globally, while also leading the cross-brand element of loyalty across Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo.

 

Reporting directly to the VP of Customer Growth & Loyalty for Brand Expedia, this role is best suited to a strategic thinker with a deep understanding of loyalty program best practices, program economics, and operational scaling.

 

You will bring a data-driven approach and an analytical mindset to dive into insights, listen to travelers, and uncover growth opportunities that ladder up to our broader organizational goals.

 

Close collaboration with Brand Expedia leadership and cross-brand partners is essential to align loyalty strategy with brand-specific goals and key performance indicators. This role regularly interfaces with executive (SVP+ and C-level) leadership as well as cross-functional partners across all levels, requiring authentic relationship-building and strong stakeholder alignment.

 

Additionally, this role proactively identifies opportunities to improve traveler journeys, elevate engagement, and strengthen brand loyalty through continuous enhancements to current offerings, prioritizing simplicity, operational rigor, and traveler comprehension.

 

Finally, this role is external-facing and engages with key strategic partners and third-party entities, fostering high-impact relationships to elevate the Brand Expedia traveler experience.

 

**In this role, you will:**

 

**Strategic Vision & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Own the vision and develop strategies to grow and strengthen customer relationships, repeat bookings, and long-term stickiness through Brand Expedia loyalty and customer growth initiatives.
* Drive a comprehensive loyalty and customer growth agenda, aligning program value propositions with short-term incentives, lifecycle touchpoints, and personalized member experiences.
* Manage and strengthen cross-functional relationships across Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo to ensure tight alignment between loyalty operations and brand strategy.
* Act as an energetic advocate for loyalty at every level, connecting program strategy back to the company's broader business objectives and ensuring loyalty has a clear voice across the organization.
* Flex effortlessly between high-level strategic vision and detailed operational execution, knowing when to dive into mechanics and when to empower your team.
* Utilize market research, customer insights, competitor intelligence, and behavioral data analytics to identify high-potential customer segments and personalize member engagement.
* Design, implement, and optimize loyalty offerings and operational workflows to ensure they deliver tangible customer value and achieve business targets.
* Serve as the dedicated voice of the traveler, partnering closely with brand marketing, product development, and member experience teams.
* Balance agile, short-term experimentation (such as rapid test-and-learn initiatives) with scalable, long-term programmatic frameworks.
* Collaborate closely with Loyalty Performance, Finance, and Analytics teams on program economics, business casing, and measurement, while partnering with Product, Technology, and Experience Design (XD) to deliver seamless end-to-end traveler journeys.
Coordinate with CRM, Integrated Marketing, Research & Insights, and commercial teams to drive cohesive execution across channels. 

 

**Team Leadership & Operational Stewardship**

* Lead, inspire, and grow a high-performing organization of 6 team members, including direct management of 3 Senior Managers, cultivating an inclusive, innovative environment with a "Go Get What's Next" mindset.
* Guide team operations, resource allocation, and project roadmaps to ensure seamless delivery across all strategic loyalty streams.
* Empower team members to move quickly, resolve roadblocks independently, and drive measurable outcomes with clarity.
* Unlock each team member's full potential, supporting individualized development paths and career progression.
* Build trust, positive momentum, and mutual accountability across the team and with executive stakeholders.
Balance workloads effectively so all team members are fully engaged and given meaningful opportunities to stretch their leadership capabilities. 

 

**Experience & Qualifications:**

* 10+ years of relevant experience in loyalty strategy, customer lifecycle marketing, or commercial growth, with a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 5+ years of demonstrated people leadership experience, with proven success managing people leaders (e.g. Senior Managers) and developing high-performing teams.
* Proven track record leading large-scale, global loyalty programs and complex operational workstreams that deliver exceptional business outcomes.
* Deep domain expertise in modern loyalty strategies, customer retention, motivational mechanics, and incentive design.
* Strong business acumen and analytical capability to interpret complex data, model program economics, and make decisive, value-generating decisions.
* Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships across diverse groups, including Product, Technology, Analytics, Finance, Supply, Brand Marketing, and Customer Operations.
* Exceptional communication and executive presence, with a proven ability to influence, socialize recommendations, and drive alignment at all leadership levels.
* Passion for designing delightful customer experiences and driving customer retention through customer-centric, data-grounded approaches.
* Thrives in a dynamic, collaborative environment, managing multiple priorities with sound judgment, adaptability, and high attention to detail.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and modern collaboration tools.
* Experience with Tableau or similar business intelligence and analytics platforms.
Proactive curiosity and ability to leverage modern AI tools to streamline processes, automate repetitive tasks, and elevate team efficiency. 

 
The total cash range for this position in New York is $224,000.00 to $313,500.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $358,500.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role.
The total cash range for this position in Seattle is $207,500.00 to $290,500.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $332,000.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role. 
 

Starting pay for this role will vary based on multiple factors, including location, available budget, and an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience. Pay ranges may be modified in the future.

 

**Benefits and perks**

Expedia Group offers benefits and perks designed to support employees and their families, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, an Employee Assistance Program, wellness and travel reimbursement, travel discounts, and International Airlines Travel Agent Network (IATAN) membership. Learn more about life at Expedia Group at https://careers.expediagroup.com/life .

 

**Accommodation requests**

Expedia Group is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruiting experience. If you need an accommodation or adjustment due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a request at https://expedia.service-now.com/askeg?id=job\_accommodation .

 

**About Expedia Group**

Expedia Group includes three flagship consumer brands - Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo - along with a leading B2B travel business and travel advertising offerings. Across our brands and business, we help travelers explore the world with confidence and ease.

 

**Important notice**

Employment opportunities and job offers at Expedia Group will always come from Expedia Group's Talent Acquisition and hiring teams. Never share sensitive personal information unless you are confident of the recipient. Expedia Group does not extend job offers via email or messaging tools to individuals with whom we have not made prior contact. Our email domain is @expediagroup.com. The official place to find and apply for roles is https://careers.expediagroup.com/jobs/ .

 

**Equal Opportunity**

Expedia is committed to creating an inclusive work environment with a diverse workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. This employer participates in E-Verify. The employer will provide the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with information from each new employee's I-9 to confirm work authorization.

records.description:
**About NYC Health + Hospitals**
--------------------------------

 

NYC Health + Hospitals is the largest public health care system in the United States. We provide essential outpatient, inpatient and home-based services to more than one million New Yorkers every year across the city’s five boroughs. Our large health system consists of ambulatory centers, acute care centers, post-acute care/long-term care, rehabilitation programs, Home Care, and Correctional Health Services. Our diverse workforce is uniquely focused on empowering New Yorkers.

At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.

**Work Shifts**
---------------

 

**9:00 A.M – 5:00 P.M**

**Duties & Responsibilities**
-----------------------------

 

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Strategic Planning

* Lead the indirect procurement function by developing and executing a comprehensive strategy to optimize spend across diverse non-clinical categories
* Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to align procurement strategies with organizational goals and operational priorities
* Utilize data analytics and market intelligence to identify opportunities for cost savings, process improvements, and supplier consolidation
* Develop operating procedures, internal policies, and training guides to support consistent procurement practices
* Partner with internal stakeholders to create scopes of work, request for proposals, and other solicitation documents

2. Operational Performance

* Oversee contracting, monitor contract compliance, and manage vendor relationships to ensure optimal pricing, service levels, and risk mitigation
* Drive cost-savings initiatives while maintaining compliance with healthcare regulations, organizational policies, and industry standards
* Manage capital procurement activities in coordination with internal and external partners throughout planning, budgeting, project management, and transactional phases
* Monitor supplier performance, manage risks, and resolve issues promptly to maintain uninterrupted service and supply
* Develop and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to savings, supplier performance, and process efficiency
* Prioritize procurement activities to meet end-user deadlines and expectations
* Develop and deliver executive briefings to senior leadership, providing insights on supply chain performance, risk mitigation, and strategic opportunities
* Perform related duties as required to support departmental and organizational objectives

3. Staff Development

* Train and lead a high-performing procurement team focused on operational excellence and professional growth
* Foster a collaborative and innovative team culture that encourages continuous learning and improvement
* Implement training programs to enhance team skills in strategic sourcing, contract management, and vendor relations
* Promote effective communication and engagement across all levels of the organization

4. Financial Management

* Lead spend reduction initiatives and ensure effective financial management of indirect procurement budgets
* Collaborate with finance and project teams to ensure accurate budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting
* Conduct procurement audits and risk assessments to maintain fiscal discipline and compliance
* Utilize financial data to track savings realization, cost avoidance, and return on investment

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

 

1. Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Computer Science,
 
Management or other related discipline from an accredited college or university; and six (6) years of satisfactory,
 
full-time paid responsible experience in information processing, program management, systems development or
 
related activity in a large governmental agency, hospital or health care facility, or hospital-related business firm,
 
three (3) years of which must have been in a managerial capacity; or
 
2. Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in disciplines, as listed in “1” above, and five (5) years of
 
experience, as described in #2 above, one (1) year of which must have been in a managerial capacity; or
 
3. A satisfactory equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Department Preferences**
--------------------------

* Indirect and Non-Clinical Spend Categories
* Strategic Sourcing
* Contract Negotiation
* Vendor Management

**Benefits**
------------

 

NYC Health and Hospitals offers a competitive benefits package that includes:

* Comprehensive Health Benefits for employees hired to work 20+ hrs. per week
* Retirement Savings and Pension Plans
* Paid Holidays and Vacation in accordance with employees' Collectively bargained contracts
* Loan Forgiveness Programs for eligible employees
* College tuition discounts and professional development opportunities
* College Savings Program
* Union Benefits for eligible titles
* Multiple employee discounts programs
* Commuter Benefits Programs

**How To Apply**
----------------

 

If you wish to apply for this position, please apply online by clicking the "Apply for Job" button.

records.description:
**About K12 Coalition**

K12 Coalition provides products and services that help K-12 schools and teachers achieve transformational learning outcomes. We tackle many of today’s toughest education obstacles, including teacher certification, test preparation, professional learning, curriculum, consulting, and strategic planning. K12 Coalition came together when educators with deep experience as teachers, school leaders, and high-level district administrators observed a genuine need for something better. Our divisions include iteach, Passage Preparation, Professional Development Institute, Teaching Channel, Lavinia Group, and Keys to Literacy.

 

**About Lavinia Group**

Lavinia Group is dedicated to driving meaningful academic improvements in K-12 education through instructional coaching, professional learning, high-quality curriculum, strategic planning, and summer school support that enhances educator effectiveness and strengthens student outcomes.

 

With deep expertise in school leadership, curriculum implementation, and instructional best practices, Lavinia Group delivers tailored, research-based solutions to meet the evolving needs of our partners. Guided by a commitment to equity, instructional excellence, and long-term capacity building, we work alongside educators and district leaders through hands-on coaching, immersive training, and collaborative partnerships. Our mission is to help schools achieve transformational learning outcomes that endure beyond our direct support.

 

**Employment Type:**

* Full-Time
* Exempt
* Salaried

 

**Location:** Remote, available from anywhere within the U.S.

 

**The Opportunity**

Lavinia Group, a division of K12 Coalition, is seeking an Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support to build and lead the systems that bring our curriculum and professional learning services to schools. The largest focus of this role is managing the full operational lifecycle of our print curriculum, from demand forecasting and inventory planning to production, fulfillment, and direct customer support. This role also leads operational planning for digital curriculum, professional learning, and consultant staffing outside of our RISE summer learning program.

 

This is an opportunity to help shape how a newly structured operations team works together. Partnering with the Managing Director, Operations and fellow operations leaders, you will help establish clear responsibilities, shared processes, and scalable systems across Lavinia Group while leading execution within your own portfolio. You will turn product and service priorities into practical plans, use technology and AI to improve workflows, and build the operational foundation for new offerings and continued growth.

 

The Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support reports to the Managing Director, Operations and directly manages a Senior Associate, Operations. This role is ideal for an operations leader who enjoys building structure, solving complex delivery challenges, and staying closely involved in day-to-day execution.

 

**What You’ll Do**

Print Curriculum & Fulfillment Operations

* Lead the full print curriculum workflow, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production schedules, ordering, and fulfillment.
* Partner with Sales and Curriculum teams to translate sales projections, partner needs, and product timelines into purchasing and production plans.
* Manage print vendors, book vendors, and fulfillment partners, including negotiations, performance monitoring, and issue resolution against quality, cost, and delivery expectations.
* Monitor inventory and fulfillment costs, anticipating shortages, excess stock, and delivery risks and adjusting plans as needs change.
* Provide direct customer support for curriculum orders and delivery questions, coordinating timely resolution of fulfillment issues and keeping partners informed.

Operational Systems & Product Implementation

* Build and improve the systems, workflows, and project plans that support curriculum and professional learning development, implementation, and delivery.
* Partner with Curriculum, Product, and Technology teams to define operational requirements for digital curriculum platforms and coordinate improvements that support users and internal teams.
* Establish consistent partner onboarding processes and coordinate operational readiness for product launches, updates, and retirements.
* Use technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools to reduce manual work, improve visibility, and create more reliable, scalable workflows.
* Partner with fellow operations leaders to establish shared practices, clarify team handoffs, and resolve dependencies across Lavinia Group.

Professional Learning & Consultant Staffing

* Lead operational planning for partner-facing professional learning and coaching services, aligning schedules, staffing, resources, and delivery requirements.
* Develop and maintain staffing and capacity plans, partnering with academic and service leaders to forecast facilitator, consultant, and content-development needs.
* Manage consultant staffing and utilization in Hub Planner, maintaining accurate assignments and availability and addressing capacity gaps with relevant leaders.
* Manage workflows for custom professional learning requests, pricing, and approvals in partnership with academic and business leaders.
* Establish operational delivery standards and monitor utilization, delivery days, and partner feedback to identify and implement improvements.

Budget & Performance Management

* Build and manage curriculum, product, and professional learning operating budgets in partnership with the Managing Director, Operations and relevant business leaders.
* Monitor spending, delivery costs, and budget performance, recommending adjustments that align resources with demand and organizational priorities.
* Maintain reporting that gives leaders clear visibility into inventory, fulfillment, staffing capacity, and operational performance.
* Coordinate with finance and sales operations colleagues to ensure accurate information and clear handoffs for invoicing, contracting, and vendor onboarding.

Team Leadership

* Manage and develop the Senior Associate, Operations, setting clear priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
* Provide ongoing coaching and feedback, delegate work effectively, and support professional growth while maintaining accountability for team deliverables.

Other Duties

* Support the team with additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to help meet evolving organizational goals and objectives.

* Bachelor’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* At least 5 years of experience in operations, product operations, supply chain, or a related field, including managing complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Direct experience managing operations for physical products sold to customers, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production or purchasing coordination, and fulfillment.
* Experience managing vendors and fulfillment partners, including monitoring costs, quality, and delivery performance and resolving customer issues.
* Demonstrated success building scalable operational systems and workflows, including defining operational requirements, partnering across teams to implement improvements, and using AI-enabled tools and automation to reduce manual work.
* Experience managing budgets, analyzing operational data, and developing staffing, capacity, or resource plans.
* Experience managing and developing direct reports, including setting priorities, delegating work, and providing performance feedback.
* Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace, particularly Google Sheets, for forecasting, reporting, data analysis, and operational decision-making, along with experience using project management or workflow tools.
* Strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate across teams, manage competing priorities, and follow through on commitments.
* Experience in K–12 education, curriculum publishing, or professional learning is preferred but not required.

**How We Work at K12 Coalition**

Our work is grounded in five Core Competencies that guide how we collaborate, support others, and move work forward: Accountability, Adaptability, Collaboration, Customer Service Orientation, and Initiative.

* **Accountability:** Following through on work, owning commitments, and communicating progress or challenges along the way.
* **Adaptability:** Navigating change with flexibility and focus as priorities, information, or needs shift.
* **Collaboration:** Working together across roles and perspectives to achieve shared goals.
* **Customer Service Orientation:** Meeting the needs of internal and external partners with clarity, responsiveness, and follow-through.
* **Initiative:** Taking action without waiting to be asked and looking for ways to improve systems, processes, or experiences.

 

**Compensation Philosophy**

As part of our commitment to maintaining fair and consistent compensation practices, new hires are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the band minimum and midpoint, based on their qualifications, location, internal alignment, and the budgeted amount for the role.

 

**Why Work with Us**

We believe in supporting the whole employee by offering a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet diverse needs. Our full-time employee benefits include flexible time off, paid parental leave, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, and a 401(k) with company matching. We are committed to fostering a work environment that promotes both personal and professional well-being.

 

**Our Typical Selection Process**

Our selection process typically includes an online application, a short phone interview, a hiring manager interview, a candidate exercise, and a final interview.

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

K12 Coalition is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you need assistance or accommodation during the interview process due to a disability, please email us at recruitingteam@k12coalition.com. This information will be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose of determining an appropriate accommodation for the interview process.

 

**Protecting Your Job Search**

K12 Coalition is committed to a transparent and secure recruitment process. Please keep the following in mind as you explore opportunities with us:

* **Official communication:** All recruitment-related communication will come from an @k12coalition.com email address. We do not use messaging platforms for recruiting.
* **Application process:** We do not send unsolicited job offers. All open positions are listed on our official Careers Page, and any offer follows a formal interview process.
* **No upfront payments:** We will never ask candidates to pay fees of any kind during the hiring process, including for training materials, background checks, or equipment.

 

If you receive any communication that does not align with the above, please report it to recruitingteam@k12coalition.com.

records.title: Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations
records.description:
**Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations**
--------------------------------------------

**Location:** Warren, MI 
**Work Model:** On-Site 
**Employment Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:**General Manager

**About SLPT**
--------------

**SLPT** is a manufacturing organization committed to delivering quality, reliability, and operational excellence for our customers. Located in Warren, Michigan, we take pride in building a culture where safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement drive everything we do.Our success starts with our people. We believe the best results come from empowered leaders who are willing to take ownership, develop talent, solve challenges, and continually raise the bar for performance. From the production floor to the leadership team, we foster an environment where employees are respected, supported, and encouraged to grow professionally.As we continue to invest in our operations, technology, and workforce, we are seeking leaders who are passionate about manufacturing excellence and motivated by the opportunity to make a measurable impact. The Plant Manager plays a critical role in shaping plant culture, driving continuous improvement, developing future leaders, and ensuring we consistently deliver exceptional results for our customers.

**Why Join SLPT?**
------------------

* Lead a high-impact manufacturing operation with significant responsibility and visibility.
* Influence plant strategy, operational performance, and business growth.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that create meaningful results.
* Partner with a collaborative leadership team focused on innovation and operational excellence.
* Develop and mentor employees while building a culture of accountability, engagement, and success.
* Join an organization that values strong leadership, problem-solving, and professional growth.

**At SLPT, you'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact on our people, our customers, and the future of our manufacturing operations.**

**About the Role**
------------------

Are you a hands-on manufacturing leader who thrives in a fast-paced production environment? We are seeking an experienced **Plant Manager**to lead all aspects of our Warren, Michigan manufacturing operation. In this role, you will oversee safety, quality, production, delivery performance, cost management, and employee development across a 24-hour operation.You will play a key role in driving operational excellence, implementing Lean Manufacturing initiatives, and developing high-performing teams while ensuring customer expectations and business objectives are consistently achieved. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership experience, a passion for continuous improvement, and a proven track record of delivering results in a multi-shift manufacturing environment.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Lead daily manufacturing operations across multiple shifts, ensuring achievement of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost goals.
* Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, urgency, and continuous improvement throughout the facility.
* Champion a zero-incident safety culture and ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, environmental standards, customer requirements, and company policies.
* Oversee production, maintenance, engineering, quality, materials, warehousing, and logistics functions.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, and operational excellence initiatives to improve efficiency, reduce waste, and maximize Operational Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).
* Monitor plant financial performance, including labor costs, operating expenses, inventory, maintenance spending, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Support successful new product launches by partnering with engineering, quality, materials, and program management teams.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions to improve quality performance, reduce scrap and rework, and enhance customer satisfaction.
* Develop leaders and employees through coaching, succession planning, workforce development, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Utilize KPIs and operational metrics to identify opportunities, solve problems, and drive sustainable business improvements.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years of experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar senior manufacturing leader.
* Proven success managing multi-shift manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated ability to achieve and sustain performance targets in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost management.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets and operational expenses.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Automotive manufacturing experience.
* Experience supporting or maintaining IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 quality systems.
* Expertise in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, Kaizen, and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Certified Manufacturing Manager (CMfgM), PMP certification, or similar professional credentials.
* Master's degree in a related discipline.

Why you'll want to join our team:

* Lead a critical manufacturing operation with broad operational responsibility.
* Make a meaningful impact on plant performance, customer satisfaction, and company growth.
* Partner with an experienced leadership team in a collaborative environment.
* Drive operational excellence and shape the future of the facility.
* Develop and mentor the next generation of manufacturing leaders.
* Influence strategic initiatives, capital investments, and continuous improvement efforts.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Competitive benefits and salary package being offered for this role.

This position is based on-site in Warren, MI and requires a strong presence on the production floor. Occasional travel may be required for customer meetings, supplier visits, training, and corporate initiatives.

records.title: Vice President, Hardware Quality
records.description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.
  
  
WHOOP is seeking a Vice President of Hardware Quality to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of quality across our global hardware ecosystem. This leader will be responsible for ensuring quality is embedded throughout the product lifecycle — from early product development through manufacturing, supplier management, and field performance. Working closely with Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Membership Services, Finance, and manufacturing partners, you will build scalable systems, drive operational excellence, and create a culture of continuous improvement that enables WHOOP to deliver exceptional products and member experiences at scale.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Define and execute a comprehensive quality strategy spanning product quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, field quality, and containment across the hardware lifecycle.
* Build, lead, and develop a world-class global quality organization that enables operational excellence and unlocks growth and scale.
* Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Product Development teams to ensure robust quality planning, validation, and risk mitigation throughout new product introduction and sustaining engineering activities.
* Establish quality metrics, operating mechanisms, and executive reporting frameworks that provide visibility into quality performance, risks, and opportunities across the supply chain.
* Drive closed-loop quality improvement initiatives by connecting field performance, reliability testing, manufacturing data, supplier performance, and product design insights.

Joining us is a chance to do important work that creates change and shapes the future of healthcare. Thinking differently is what we do best. To us, change equals opportunity. The VP, Corporate Quality Systems is a key member of the Quality Leadership Team (QLT) with responsibility to design, implement and oversee the Integra Global quality system, including identifying compliance improvement and remediation strategies across Integra LifeSciences. This role will work cross-functionally across all Integra facilities to build an integrated Quality system infrastructure that supports continued compliance across Integra sites. This role is crucial for ensuring the development, manufacture, and distribution of medical devices in compliance with corporate policies, U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulations, ISO 13485, the Canadian Medical Device Regulations (CMDR), the EU Medical Device Regulation, Japanese Pharmaceutical Affairs Law, and other applicable regulatory agencies.
  
  
**SUPERVISION RECEIVED**

**SUPERVISION EXCERCISED**
Directly manages a Quality system corporate team (CAPA, NCE, Doc Control, Management Controls, Training/L&D, Audit/Compliance, Corporate Headquarters Site Quality, and Post Market Surveillance).
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Build a high-performance quality culture and team, empowering and holding direct reports and cross-functional teams accountable for successful quality and compliance transformation. Leads with authority and influences globally across manufacturing and distribution facilities and cross functional stakeholders including but not limited to quality, product development, process technology, operations, supply chain, procurement, regulatory affairs, finance, and human resources.

**Description**

**Company & Job Overview:**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Manufacturing is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in Operations leadership, particularly in a medical device, medical technology or biotechnology organization. They will possess deep expertise in talent management, organizational development, and workforce planning.

This position is an office-based position at the company’s Irvine, CA headquarters.

**Travel**

This position primarily works in an office environment. It requires frequent sitting, standing and walking. Daily use of a computer and other computing and digital devices is required. May stand for extended periods when facilitating meetings or walking in the facilities.

In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification
* Experience with AS9100 quality systems
* Capital project management experience (multi-million dollar equipment investments)
* Experience taking spacecraft products into production, including progressive design iterations to reduce delivered cost
* Demonstrated experience applying system engineering practices to AIT operations
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging directly with customers in technical/proposal settings
* Experience working directly with customers in the commercial space industry
* Ability to work independently with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

records.description:
**Company Background and Summary**

Votaw Precision Technologies is a trusted leader in the manufacturing of complex precision components, assemblies, and systems for the aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors. With a strong reputation for technical excellence, quality craftsmanship, and on-time delivery, Votaw supports some of the world’s most demanding programs through its advanced manufacturing capabilities. The company specializes in precision machining, fabrication, welding, and complex assembly operations for mission-critical applications. Votaw Precision Technologies has long been a trusted partner in building mission-critical hardware for some of the most advanced aerospace and defense programs in the world. Our precision components support the International Space Station, nearly every major launch vehicle in operation, high-performance spacecraft (including classified missions), as well as next-generation fighter aircraft, bombers, submarines, radar systems, and ground vehicles.

We are seeking an experienced and highly knowledgeable Operations Director to lead the overall operations of a high-performance CNC machine shop. This individual will have full responsibility for the day-to-day management, technical excellence, production performance, staffing, scheduling, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the facility.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned machining professional with approximately 20 years of industry experience who understands metal cutting and CNC machining at a deep technical level and has progressed into a strong operational leadership role.

The Operations Director must be able to walk onto the shop floor, understand the machining challenges, evaluate processes, communicate effectively with machinists and programmers, identify inefficiencies, and make sound technical and operational decisions. The company utilizes a variety of CNC machining technologies, including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining, as well as vertical milling, welding and large-scale assembly tooling.

**Essential Functions**

* Responsible for ensuring that the entire organization operates safely, efficiently, profitably, and to the highest standards of quality and technical excellence.
* Have overall responsibility for the day-to-day operations of the CNC machine shop.
* Establish and maintain a culture of technical excellence, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Provide leadership and direction to machining, programming, production, quality, maintenance, and other shop personnel.
* Ensure the shop has the appropriate personnel, equipment, tooling, processes, and resources to meet customer requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for supervisors, leads, machinists, programmers, and support personnel.
* Serve as the primary operational leader and decision maker for the manufacturing facility.
* Work closely with programmers, machinists, and engineers to resolve technical machining issues.
* Evaluate machining processes and identify opportunities to improve cycle time, tool life, throughput, and quality.
* Ensure manufacturing processes are technically sound, repeatable, and scalable.
* Provide technical guidance when difficult or complex machining problems arise.
* Maintain an environment where machinists, engineers, programmers continuously improve their technical capabilities.
* Responsible for weld shop, tooling assembly, and manufacturing readiness team.

**Qualifications and Skills**

* Approximately 20 years of experience in the CNC machining/manufacturing industry.
* Previous experience as a Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Operations Manager, Plant Manager, Production Manager, or Director of Operations.
* Experience managing multiple shifts and 24/7 operations
* Knowledge of complex, tight-tolerance, or high-value machined components.
* Experience with 5-axis machining and advanced CNC manufacturing.
* Implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Knowledge of ERP/MRP and production scheduling systems.
* Managing capital equipment purchases and machine capacity planning.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, automotive, or other high-precision manufacturing environments is a plus.

**Personal Attributes**

* Highly self-motivated and directed.
* Keen attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.
* Ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented, collaborative environment.

**Work Conditions**

* Ability to work onsite, including hours outside of a normal working day, to meet critical deadlines.
* This position operates within a precision manufacturing environment supporting the production of mission-critical aerospace and defense components. Success requires a high sense of urgency, attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple departments to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and customer delivery commitments.
* Ability to work safely in a manufacturing environment, including walking the production floor, climbing stairs or ladders, occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).

**Additional Requirements**

* This position requires the use of information or access to hardware subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by ITAR.

***Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.***

Demonstrated ability to interpret operational and financial data, evaluate performance trends, and leverage technology to support strategic planning and informed decision-making.

Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.
  
  
In addition to the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), we offer a flexible work environment, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, industry competitive compensation, and superior benefits to include medical, dental, 401k and more!
  
  
ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!
  
  
**Position Summary**
ASI is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Production to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of its production organization. This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.
  
  
Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.
  
  
This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
*Strategic Leadership & Operational Management*

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing.
* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Oversee production planning, scheduling, capacity management, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent programs.
* Partner with Program Management and Engineering to translate contractual requirements and technical specifications into executable production plans.
* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.
* Provide production estimates, labor forecasts, capacity assessments, and schedule inputs for new business proposals.

*Manufacturing & Systems Integration*

* Oversee the manufacturing and assembly of complex simulation and training device hardware.
* Ensure effective collaboration between Production and Engineering to promote manufacturability, reliability, and cost-effective designs.
* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.
* Drive improvements in production flow, manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and delivery performance.

*Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.
* Promote accurate material tracking and accountability through ASI's ERP system.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.

* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.

We're an EV commercial vehicle manufacturer based in Orange County, California. We design and build our medium-duty electric vehicles in-house, and next year's production is already fully sold out.

* 1,000+ vehicles built so far
* A 2,000-vehicle order from one of the largest US parcel carriers, due by end of 2027

* Growing beyond trucks into energy storage, autonomy and defense

The role

We've sold out of trucks, and we don't want it to happen again. We're hiring a
**Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering**
to grow our production capacity and own how we get there.

You'll lead the team that designs, buys and launches our new lines and equipment. Your decisions will show up directly in how many trucks leave the factory each month.

What you'll do

* Lead and grow the advanced manufacturing engineering team

records.description:
**About Varda**
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
**Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
  
  
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
  
  
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
  
  
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
  
  
**About This Role**
As the
**Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)**
at Varda, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the mission-critical payload systems that define what Varda's reentry capsules actually do in space. Varda's payloads — including pharmaceutical processing hardware, microgravity experiment modules, and government and commercial customer systems — represent the core value proposition of every mission. You will translate payload design requirements into production-ready assembly processes, develop rigorous work instructions, and work hands-on with technicians to ensure payloads are built, integrated, and verified to the highest standards of quality and cleanliness. This role demands both technical breadth and meticulous process discipline: you will interface with external payload customers, internal design teams, and the vehicle integration team to ensure every payload is ready to fly. If you are driven by the idea that what you manufacture will directly enable life-saving pharmaceuticals or cutting-edge scientific research in microgravity, this role is for you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Own end-to-end manufacturing and assembly processes for Varda payload systems, including pharmaceutical processing hardware, experiment modules, and customer-furnished payload equipment
* Develop and maintain detailed work instructions, assembly travelers, process specifications, and acceptance test procedures for payload fabrication and integration operations
* Serve as the primary manufacturing interface for payload customers, translating customer requirements and ICD (Interface Control Document) constraints into executable production processes
* Implement contamination control, cleanliness, and handling protocols appropriate for sensitive payload hardware, including pharmaceutical-grade and precision optical components
* Collaborate with payload design engineers to provide DFM and DFA feedback on assembly accessibility, connector placement, thermal interface design, and testability
* Define and execute payload acceptance testing, functional verification checkouts, and pre-integration inspections; maintain complete and traceable build records
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for payload non-conformances; coordinate MRB dispositions with design engineering and, where applicable, payload customers
* Coordinate payload integration milestones with the vehicle integration team, ensuring payload readiness gates align with overall vehicle build schedule

**Basic Qualifications**

* B.S. in Mechanical, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)
* 6+ years of experience manufacturing or integrating complex and compact electromechanical assemblies, scientific instruments, or payload systems in aerospace, defense, biomedical, or research environments
* Demonstrated experience building and integrating precision hardware to tight tolerances and exacting cleanliness requirements
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, ICDs, and assembly models; familiarity with GD&T and interface requirement management
* Experience developing and executing assembly procedures and acceptance test plans for multi-functional hardware assemblies
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable interfacing directly with customers and cross-functional internal teams
* Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Fluid Mechanics, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline
* Experience manufacturing or integrating spacecraft payloads, scientific instruments, or hosted payload modules for LEO, GEO, or deep space missions
* Familiarity with pharmaceutical or bioprocessing hardware manufacturing requirements, including GMP considerations and contamination control protocols relevant to in-space drug manufacturing
* Background managing payload customer relationships from hardware delivery through integration, verification, and launch readiness
* Experience with ICD management and interface verification processes for payload-to-spacecraft integration
* Knowledge of microgravity experiment hardware design considerations and their manufacturing implications
* Familiarity with environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration, shock) as it applies to payload hardware acceptance and qualification
* Experience working in or adjacent to a cleanroom environment (ISO Class 7 or better) for integration of sensitive flight payloads
* Prior work at a company developing commercial space services with a direct end-user product — pharmaceutical, government, or research — where manufacturing quality directly impacted mission outcome

Pay Range
  
  

* Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements
  
  
Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.
  
  
“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).
