**Join the Clean Energy Revolution**

  

Become a **Senior Manager, Demand Side Management Quality Assurance & Engineering** at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this role, you’ll lead a regulatory (policy) engineering team that conducts technical reviews, researches and develops new technologies, and works closely with the CPUC and industry experts to advance energy efficiency. Because you’ll oversee the quality control of program implementations and ensure their compliance, ideally your background would include Demand Side Management (DSM), such as Energy Efficiency, Demand Response, Integrated Demand Side Management, and Distributed Energy Resources.

  

As a **Senior Manager, Demand Side Management Quality Assurance & Engineering**, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

  

**Incident Management Team Expected Participation**: Employees are expected to support emergency response and/or business continuity efforts, including readiness to serve on an Incident Management Team (IMT) when needed. Employees will participate in an on-call rotation (approximately every four to six weeks), to support IMT activations during emergency events. IMT assignments may differ from an individual’s regular responsibilities.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Leads a variety of engineering and business initiatives to develop grid strategies, determine how the grid is planned, designed, operated and maintained to operationalize company's strategy
* Manages and prioritizes the engineering roadmap in collaboration with other departments; develops and implements strategies for improving execution efficiency
* Leads, manages and supports the project engineering group and remains responsible and accountable for their team's delivery of small to large scale projects
* Manages execution performance of their teams, identifying barriers, and prioritizing work for their teams to ensure projects are delivered on-time, within scope and within budgets
* Reviews and makes decisions on project plans, resource allocation, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, budgets, and resources to ensure timely and successful delivery of capital and strategic projects Oversee the development and implementation of a comprehensive project management framework to ensure efficient project execution, reporting, and delivery of goals within budget
* Drives the adoption of digitalization and automation technologies to improve engineering processes, reduce manual effort, and enhance project outcomes
* Leads the development and maintains a robust risk management strategy to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with engineering projects
* Develops goals and assigns projects/roles to employees that translate corporate strategic vision into actionable initiatives to delegate.
* Leads the development and implementation of cross organizational strategy, technology and safety program to ensure company advancement toward future vision and the well-being of employees and contractors involved in engineering projects
* A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

* Five or more years of experience supervising a team of direct reports and/or project management.
* Experience performing engineering work in operations, production, construction or maintenance environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

  

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in business administration, engineering (mechanical, electrical, or environmental), or a related scientific or technical field.
* Five or more years of experience managing an organization and/or complex DSM policy and regulatory projects involving multiple stakeholders, including the CPUC.
* Three or more years of experience leading engineering or technical projects.
* Three or more years of experience managing vendors and coordinating with technical staff and consultants.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.
* Experience with DSM programs, including Energy Efficiency, Demand Response, Integrated Demand Side Management, or Distributed Energy Resources.

* This position’s work mode is **hybrid.** The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California. Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The people at SCE don't just keep the lights on. Our mission is so much bigger. We’re fueling the kind of innovation that’s changing an entire industry, and quite possibly the planet. records.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

In this role, you will guide enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen operational performance, enhance quality, and increase efficiency across multiple manufacturing sites. You will lead efforts that reduce waste, improve process capability, and support teams in optimizing complex aerospace and defense production workflows, helping ensure mission-critical hardware is delivered with consistent excellence.

#### **Duties/Responsibilities**

* Develops and deploys a multi-site continuous improvement roadmap aligned with corporate objectives.
* Leads lean, six sigma, and value stream mapping initiatives to drive operational excellence.
* Identifies and eliminates non value added activities across machining, fabrication, and downstream processing.
* Develops, tracks, and reports enterprise metrics for cost savings, yield improvements, and cycle time reduction.
* Partners with manufacturing engineering, quality, and supply chain to improve process capabilities.
* Facilitates advanced root cause problem solving activities to address systemic production bottlenecks.
* Plans and executes kaizen events focused on setup reduction, 5S workplace organization, and cellular manufacturing.
* Mentors and develops employees in lean and six sigma methodologies.
* Ensures continuous improvement initiatives support and maintain AS9100 and product safety standards.

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, or a related technical field.
* Minimum 8-10 years of operations or continuous improvement leadership in aerospace and defense manufacturing.
* Certified lean six sigma master black belt or black belt.
* Experience with AS9100 quality management systems and defense contract management agency (DCMA) oversight.
* Background in precision machining, structural fabrication, or aerospace assemblies.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and manufacturing execution system (MES) data analysis.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of business administration (MBA) or master's degree.

#### **Special Mentions**

* Travel is required across regional manufacturing sites.

#### **Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health savings account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible spending accounts (FSA)
* Company-paid life and AD&D insurance

records.title: Vice President, Hardware Quality
records.description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.
  
  
WHOOP is seeking a Vice President of Hardware Quality to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of quality across our global hardware ecosystem. This leader will be responsible for ensuring quality is embedded throughout the product lifecycle — from early product development through manufacturing, supplier management, and field performance. Working closely with Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Membership Services, Finance, and manufacturing partners, you will build scalable systems, drive operational excellence, and create a culture of continuous improvement that enables WHOOP to deliver exceptional products and member experiences at scale.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Define and execute a comprehensive quality strategy spanning product quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, field quality, and containment across the hardware lifecycle.
* Build, lead, and develop a world-class global quality organization that enables operational excellence and unlocks growth and scale.
* Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Product Development teams to ensure robust quality planning, validation, and risk mitigation throughout new product introduction and sustaining engineering activities.
* Establish quality metrics, operating mechanisms, and executive reporting frameworks that provide visibility into quality performance, risks, and opportunities across the supply chain.
* Drive closed-loop quality improvement initiatives by connecting field performance, reliability testing, manufacturing data, supplier performance, and product design insights.
* Lead supplier quality programs, including qualification processes, factory audits, corrective and preventive actions, and strategic supplier development efforts across a global manufacturing network.

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of leadership experience in hardware quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or related functions supporting consumer electronics, wearable technology, or other complex hardware products.
* Demonstrated success building and scaling high-performing quality organizations in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
* Deep understanding of consumer electronics manufacturing processes, including electro-mechanical assemblies, PCB/SMT manufacturing, batteries, plastics, and critical component qualification.
* Experience working with global manufacturing and supplier partners and managing quality across geographically distributed operations.
* Expertise in quality systems and methodologies, including statistical process control, auditing, corrective and preventive action programs, root cause analysis, FMEA, Design for Manufacturing, Lean manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
* Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence decisions through data-driven insights and cross-functional partnership.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% internationally to support manufacturing partners, suppliers, and quality initiatives.
* Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

***This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.***

records.description:
Changing lives. Building Careers.
  
  
Joining us is a chance to do important work that creates change and shapes the future of healthcare. Thinking differently is what we do best. To us, change equals opportunity. Every day, our colleagues are challenging what’s possible and making headway to innovate new treatment pathways to advance patient outcomes and set new standards of care.
  
  
**Summary**
The VP, Corporate Quality Systems is a key member of the Quality Leadership Team (QLT) with responsibility to design, implement and oversee the Integra Global quality system, including identifying compliance improvement and remediation strategies across Integra LifeSciences. This role will work cross-functionally across all Integra facilities to build an integrated Quality system infrastructure that supports continued compliance across Integra sites. This role is crucial for ensuring the development, manufacture, and distribution of medical devices in compliance with corporate policies, U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulations, ISO 13485, the Canadian Medical Device Regulations (CMDR), the EU Medical Device Regulation, Japanese Pharmaceutical Affairs Law, and other applicable regulatory agencies.
  
  
**SUPERVISION RECEIVED**
Reports to the Chief Quality Officer.
  
  
**SUPERVISION EXCERCISED**
Directly manages a Quality system corporate team (CAPA, NCE, Doc Control, Management Controls, Training/L&D, Audit/Compliance, Corporate Headquarters Site Quality, and Post Market Surveillance).
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily as follows:
  
  

* Build a high-performance quality culture and team, empowering and holding direct reports and cross-functional teams accountable for successful quality and compliance transformation. Leads with authority and influences globally across manufacturing and distribution facilities and cross functional stakeholders including but not limited to quality, product development, process technology, operations, supply chain, procurement, regulatory affairs, finance, and human resources.
* Develop organizational design and governance to achieve success. Provide strategic direction and communication of the quality transformation goals, creating a clear vision and integration with overall business objectives. Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess the effectiveness of quality and compliance remediation. Highlighting trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Leads the design, execution and evolution of the Global Quality System for Integra in conjunction with the Compliance Master Plan (CMP) team, requiring cross-functional collaboration and understanding of various roles within the organization.
* Support interactions with regulatory bodies and ensure compliance with all applicable quality and safety standards. Responsible for leading the team with the review and finalizing any responses to regulatory authorities in collaboration with the Chief Quality Officer.
* Lead the identification, analysis, and resolution of quality issues and non-conformities across various departments in collaboration with the Quality Systems and CAPA teams. Ensure remediation efforts are managed through the QMS.
* Foster a culture of quality and continuous improvement within the organization. Promote the use of lean and Six Sigma methodologies to enhance quality and operational efficiency. Stay abreast of industry trends and advancements in quality management and remediation practices.
* Guide the activities required of the quality organization to ensure compliance with all appropriate regulations and standards, including FDA Part 820, ISO 13485, CMDR, MDR, MDSAP, and JPAL. Ensures compliance and readiness globally in collaboration with the QMS.

**Qualifications And Experience Requirements**
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for this position:
  
  

* Bachelor's degree is required, in engineering, science or closely related technical discipline is preferred. A master’s degree preferred.
* 18+ years of experience leading a team (direct reports or projects) or equivalent education and years of management experience
* Experience in highly regulated industries required, medical device and/or pharmaceutical preferred, including material remediation experience
* Strong analytical skills, exceptional writing and interpersonal relationship skills or a combination of relevant work experience and education.
* Demonstrated knowledge of FDA regulations, ISO 13485, CMDR, Medical Device Directive Regulation (93/42EEC), Japanese Pharmaceutical Affairs Law, and other national and international regulations and standards.
* Experience with direct contact with FDA and EU Notified Bodies.
* Knowledge of process design and implementation, change control, auditing, and document management systems required, general knowledge of statistical analysis preferred.
* Demonstrated organizational, management and communication skills. Proven track record of cross-functional collaboration across teams and change management skills. Strong ability to influence across all levels of the organization, including senior leadership. Experienced with interacting with Executive leadership to execute decisions and manage risk.
* Ability to travel up to 50% if needed based on site needs. Regular on-site presence in Massachusetts and New Jersey facilities.

**PERSONAL COMPETENCIES**
As a senior leadership position in the company, the role is expected to demonstrate on all Integra Leadership Capabilities.
  
  

* Enterprise Mindset: Leaders with this capability make decisions, set priorities, and share resources based on what will benefit Integra as a whole.
* Thought Leadership: Leaders with this capability build personal credibility and utilize business acumen and customer mindset to influence the innovation and growth of the business. Works with a high level of strategic thinking.
* Drive Performance: Leaders with this capability drive performance and accountability through others and self.
* Enable Talent: Leaders with this capability strive to engage, support, and develop self and others, optimizing the success of individuals and teams and are experienced in dealing with change management.

**Description**

**Company & Job Overview:**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Manufacturing is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in Operations leadership, particularly in a medical device, medical technology or biotechnology organization. They will possess deep expertise in talent management, organizational development, and workforce planning.

This position is an office-based position at the company’s Irvine, CA headquarters.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Execution**

* Translate corporate vision into actionable operational strategies, setting short- and long-term objectives for scaling manufacturing and supply chain.
* Oversee Profit & Loss (P&L) for the operations division, managing budgets, and identifying areas for continuous cost optimization.
* Serve as a core member of the executive leadership team, collaborating cross-functionally with R&D, Quality, Regulatory, and Commercial teams.

* Direct all manufacturing operations (internal facilities and/or outsourced/CMO partnerships), ensuring production schedules are met with the highest standards of safety and quality.

* Implement Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce lead times, and improve manufacturing efficiency.

* Partner closely with Quality/Regulatory to uphold and enforce compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, and other global regulatory requirements.

* Partner closely with R&D during the design transfer phase to ensure new products are manufacturable, cost-effective, and ready for commercial scale.

records.description:
Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification

With a strong reputation for technical excellence, quality craftsmanship, and on-time delivery, Votaw supports some of the world’s most demanding programs through its advanced manufacturing capabilities. The company specializes in precision machining, fabrication, welding, and complex assembly operations for mission-critical applications. Votaw Precision Technologies has long been a trusted partner in building mission-critical hardware for some of the most advanced aerospace and defense programs in the world. Our precision components support the International Space Station, nearly every major launch vehicle in operation, high-performance spacecraft (including classified missions), as well as next-generation fighter aircraft, bombers, submarines, radar systems, and ground vehicles.

We are seeking an experienced and highly knowledgeable Operations Director to lead the overall operations of a high-performance CNC machine shop. This individual will have full responsibility for the day-to-day management, technical excellence, production performance, staffing, scheduling, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the facility.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned machining professional with approximately 20 years of industry experience who understands metal cutting and CNC machining at a deep technical level and has progressed into a strong operational leadership role.

The Operations Director must be able to walk onto the shop floor, understand the machining challenges, evaluate processes, communicate effectively with machinists and programmers, identify inefficiencies, and make sound technical and operational decisions. The company utilizes a variety of CNC machining technologies, including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining, as well as vertical milling, welding and large-scale assembly tooling.

**Essential Functions**

* Responsible for ensuring that the entire organization operates safely, efficiently, profitably, and to the highest standards of quality and technical excellence.
* Have overall responsibility for the day-to-day operations of the CNC machine shop.
* Establish and maintain a culture of technical excellence, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Provide leadership and direction to machining, programming, production, quality, maintenance, and other shop personnel.
* Ensure the shop has the appropriate personnel, equipment, tooling, processes, and resources to meet customer requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for supervisors, leads, machinists, programmers, and support personnel.
* Serve as the primary operational leader and decision maker for the manufacturing facility.
* Work closely with programmers, machinists, and engineers to resolve technical machining issues.
* Evaluate machining processes and identify opportunities to improve cycle time, tool life, throughput, and quality.
* Ensure manufacturing processes are technically sound, repeatable, and scalable.
* Provide technical guidance when difficult or complex machining problems arise.
* Maintain an environment where machinists, engineers, programmers continuously improve their technical capabilities.
* Responsible for weld shop, tooling assembly, and manufacturing readiness team.

**Qualifications and Skills**

* Approximately 20 years of experience in the CNC machining/manufacturing industry.
* Previous experience as a Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Operations Manager, Plant Manager, Production Manager, or Director of Operations.
* Experience managing multiple shifts and 24/7 operations
* Knowledge of complex, tight-tolerance, or high-value machined components.
* Experience with 5-axis machining and advanced CNC manufacturing.
* Implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Knowledge of ERP/MRP and production scheduling systems.
* Managing capital equipment purchases and machine capacity planning.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, automotive, or other high-precision manufacturing environments is a plus.

**Personal Attributes**

* Highly self-motivated and directed.
* Keen attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.
* Ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented, collaborative environment.

**Work Conditions**

* Ability to work onsite, including hours outside of a normal working day, to meet critical deadlines.
* This position operates within a precision manufacturing environment supporting the production of mission-critical aerospace and defense components. Success requires a high sense of urgency, attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple departments to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and customer delivery commitments.
* Ability to work safely in a manufacturing environment, including walking the production floor, climbing stairs or ladders, occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).

**Additional Requirements**

* This position requires the use of information or access to hardware subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by ITAR.

***Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.***

**Job Description**
The Director PMO NPI/NPD is responsible for leading the successful transition of new products from R&D into scalable volume manufacturing. Sitting within the PMO and reporting to the VP of Production Engineering and Continuous Improvement (PECI), this role owns NPI execution, manufacturing readiness, and phase-gate milestone delivery across the product portfolio. The Director partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management to ensure products transition seamlessly into volume manufacturing — meeting customer, quality, cost, and delivery expectations — while building the processes, tooling, and team capabilities needed to scale.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**New Product Development & Launch**

* Own PLM milestone tracking, phase-gate execution, and portfolio pipeline alignment to ensure timely and effective product launches
* Drive product commercialization from R&D handoff through launch, ensuring new products meet or exceed customer, quality, cost, and delivery requirements
* Align cross-functionally on the new product pipeline and launch readiness across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management

**Manufacturing Readiness & Scale-Up**

* Lead the transition of products from R&D into volume manufacturing, establishing scalable and repeatable production processes
* Develop and ramp manufacturing capability and capacity for new products at the R&D site
* Establish and continuously improve the R&D production line to support prototype and pilot builds

**Automation, Tooling & Test**

* Lead automation initiatives including tooling, test fixtures, and production test requirement definition
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to ensure test and tooling solutions are scalable for volume production

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of Technical Program Managers and the Engineering Manager for Prototype and Pilot Builds
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement within the NPD PMO function

**Skill & Abilities**
**Ownership & Accountability**
Ability to drive NPI program outcomes from R&D handoff through volume manufacturing launch. Holds themselves and their team to commitments, drives decisions, and escalates risks proactively — ensuring programs stay on track.
  
  
**Program & Portfolio Management**
Ability to manage multiple NPI programs simultaneously across the portfolio, maintaining phase-gate discipline, milestone ownership, and pipeline visibility from commercialization through volume launch.
  
  
**Commercialization & NPI Execution**
Ability to take products through the commercialization phase — from R&D handoff to volume manufacturing — on time and within cost, quality, and delivery targets.
  
  
**Manufacturing & Production Readiness**
Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, scale-up requirements, tooling, automation, and test development — with the ability to translate R&D outputs into production-ready solutions.
  
  
**Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence**
Ability to align and drive execution across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management without direct authority over all stakeholders — critical in a PMO structure.
  
  
**Strategic Thinking & Prioritization**
Ability to manage competing program priorities at the portfolio level, make sound trade-off decisions, and keep initiatives aligned to business objectives.
  
  
**Team Development**
Ability to lead, develop and effectively scale a team to ensure the right capabilities and resourcing are in place at the right time.
  
  
**Stakeholder Communication & Reporting**
Ability to synthesize program status, risks, and decisions into clear, concise communication for senior leadership and the c-suite.
  
  
**Travel**
Ability to travel 10-20%
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field
* 15+ years of program management experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment, with a focus on new product introduction (NPI), product transitions, or manufacturing scale-up
* 5+ years of team leadership/management role within a PMO, R&D, or Operations function
* Proven experience leading cross-functional initiatives across R&D, Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain

* Familiarity with PLM systems and phase-gate product development processes

**About Us**
Chefman is one of North America's leading brands of small kitchen appliances, committed to building best-in-class products that make cooking accessible and enjoyable. In 2020, we launched CHEF iQ, an ecosystem of connected smart kitchen appliances designed to transform how the world cooks through intuitive guided cooking experiences and IoT-enabled technology.
  
  
**About The Role**
As Chefman continues to scale, we're looking for a Director of Overseas Manufacturing and Quality to elevate how we partner with our overseas manufacturing network and ensure our growing product portfolio is built with the consistency and precision our customers expect.
  
  
This is not a desk job. We need a leader who has personally run a factory floor, someone who can walk into an assembly line, spot a process problem before it becomes a quality escape, and work directly with factory teams to fix it. You'll serve as the critical bridge between our design and product development teams here in Mahwah and our manufacturing partners in China, helping ensure that what we design translates seamlessly into what gets built at scale.
  
  
We're looking for a leader with deep, sustained manufacturing expertise, ideally 10 to 15 years building that expertise with one organization, who is ready to bring that experience to a fast-growing, entrepreneurial consumer brand. This role requires extensive travel to China and a genuine passion for being present where products come to life.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing strategy and execution across our overseas partner network, from tooling and assembly process design through high-volume mass production
* Partner early and often with Product Development and Industrial Design teams, bringing manufacturing expertise directly into design decisions to support manufacturability, cost efficiency, and quality from day one
* Champion consistency and best-practice alignment across factory SOPs, assembly procedures, and quality control standards across all manufacturing partners
* Maintain a strong, regular presence on assembly lines, staying close to daily production and building the kind of trusted, collaborative relationships with factory teams that drive continuous improvement
* Build and maintain rigorous reporting and documentation systems that give leadership clear visibility into yield, quality performance, and production trends across all partner sites
* Lead structured root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone) when quality or performance opportunities arise, partnering closely with factory teams to implement durable, lasting solutions
* Serve as the senior point of contact for resolving complex production challenges, balancing quality, cost, and delivery priorities
* Build and develop a team of manufacturing and quality engineers to support the company's growing production needs
* Evaluate and help develop new manufacturing partnerships and capacity as the business scales

**Qualifications**

* A demonstrated track record of driving measurable improvements to product quality, yield, and profitability through close factory partnership
* Deep, working-level understanding of injection molding, sheet metal, electromechanical assembly, and tooling processes, built through genuine hands-on experience
* Strong background in structured root-cause problem solving and driving continuous improvement initiatives with manufacturing partners
* Experience developing and aligning SOPs and best practices across multiple factory sites
* A natural inclination to stay close to product design conversations and offer manufacturing perspective early in the process

* Willingness and ability to travel extensively to China, including extended stays as needed

Enterprise Influence & Collaboration

Center of Excellence Leadership

Capital & Technology Strategy

* Reduced waste, scrap, and conversion costs
* Improved process capability and product quality
* Strong capital project return and benefit realization

**Qualifications**
Education & Experience
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, industrial, chemical, manufacturing engineering, or related discipline, required.
* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing, process engineering, or operational excellence leadership experience.
* Experience leading engineering teams in a multi-site (>10 sites) manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting large-scale operational transformation, capital investments, and manufacturing modernization/automation efforts.

records.description:
**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

**Equal Opportunity Statement:**
Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. The director oversees the development of data‑driven systems and processes that strengthen decision‑making, transparency, and compliance across a 1,000‑person defense manufacturing facility. records.title: Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
records.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

* Own the ISC End-to-End process architecture, defining process standards, documentation requirements, and governance for core ISC value streams.
* Drive process modeling and SIPOC-level design across ISC, working through the Process Modeler and Global Process Owner to ensure clarity of accountability and performance standards.
* Identify and close process design gaps that create risk, inefficiency, or measurement inconsistency across the ISC organization.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Define the Manufacturing Excellence framework for Nouryon, including OEE, TPM, reliability, and asset performance standards applied across the manufacturing network.
* Direct the Manufacturing Excellence Manager to develop and deploy site-level improvement programs, closing the loop between plant performance data and structured intervention.
* Integrate manufacturing excellence priorities into the broader OpEx roadmap, ensuring alignment with Digital Manufacturing, Palantir-enabled analytics, and capital investment decisions.

**People Leadership & COE Development**

* Lead a geographically distributed team of nine direct reports
* Define team structure, role clarity, and succession priorities for the COE
* Build a high-performance COE culture grounded in Nouryon’s Leadership Capability Framework

This role requires approximately 15–25% global travel across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
**Key Performance Indicators**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence COE is measured against the same Breakthrough KPIs as the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing. This alignment is intentional – the COE’s organizational design, capability systems, and governance structures exist to enable these outcomes. Execution is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role is accountable for building and sustaining the organization capable of delivering them.
  

* People Safety
* Process Safety
* FMC — Fixed Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* VMC — Variable Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* OEE — Overall Equipment Effectiveness
* OTIF — On-Time In-Full
* Quality Sigma Level
* CI Activation Rate

**We believe you bring**

* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement, or manufacturing leadership roles in a global, multi-site environment.
* Certified Master Black Belt (MBB) or Black Belt in Lean/Six Sigma, with demonstrated capability to design, govern, and quality-assure a full belt certification program.
* Proven track record of leading change management initiatives in large, matrixed, multi-regional organizations – with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and shift organizational culture.
* Deep knowledge of Manufacturing Excellence frameworks including OEE, TPM, and reliability methodologies, with experience deploying these at scale across a manufacturing network.
* Demonstrated people leadership across multiple geographies and organizational grades, including experience developing high-performing teams in a distributed structure.

**Great if you have**

* Experience in specialty chemicals, process manufacturing, or a similarly regulated, capital-intensive industrial environment.
* Hands-on expertise in End-to-End process design and governance, including SIPOC-level architecture and process ownership models.
* Experience designing and leading corporate Learning & Development programs, including competency frameworks and structured curricula for technical disciplines.
* Prior experience building or structuring a Center of Excellence from the ground up, including team design, governance models, and stakeholder alignment.
* Working proficiency with PowerBI or equivalent reporting platforms for program performance tracking and executive communication.

**We believe you are**
...
  
  
A systems thinker who sees the whole before diving into the parts. You lead through frameworks, not firefighting – you understand that durable operational excellence is built on governance, capability, and culture, not individual heroics. You bring intellectual rigor to every conversation and are comfortable challenging assumptions at any level of the organization, including in rooms where the answer is already assumed.
  
  
You are energized by building – building teams, building programs, building the conditions for others to succeed. You know how to hold standards without being rigid, and how to drive urgency without creating chaos. The right candidate is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in watching a global organization improve because of the systems they put in place – and who brings the patience, persistence, and precision that transformation at scale demands.
  
  
**We offer you**
This is a rare opportunity to architect and lead a newly consolidated global COE with a clear mandate from senior leadership, a defined team, and direct line of sight to enterprise value delivery. You will operate with significant autonomy, build the structure you believe is right, and leave a measurable legacy across a global manufacturing organization at an inflection point in its CI and digital transformation journey.
  
  
At Nouryon, we provide a great job and friendly coworkers, plus benefits in addition to salary.
  
  
**Have we got your interest?**
This is a permanent position on a full-time basis, reporting to VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub Amsterdam, Netherlands | Houston, TX, USA
  
  
Please apply via our online recruitment system. We will not accept applications via e-mail. Once it's with us we will review to see if we have a match between your skills and the role! For more information about our hiring process, visit: nouryon.com/careers/how-we-hire/
  
  
We look forward to receiving your application!
  
  
We kindly ask our internal candidates to apply with your Nouryon email via Success Factors.
  
  
**About Nouryon**
Explore careers and life at Nouryon
  
  
If you’re looking for your next career move, apply today and join Nouryon’s worldwide team in providing essential solutions that our customers use to manufacture everyday products such as personal care, cleaning, paints and coatings, agriculture and food, pharmaceuticals, and building products. Our employees are driven by the wish to make an impact and actively drive positive change. If that describes you, we will gladly make way for your ambitions. From day one we support you with your personal growth, through challenging positions and comprehensive learning and development opportunities, in a dynamic, international, diverse, and proactive working environment.
  
  
Visit our website and follow us on LinkedIn .
  
  
**#WeAreNouryon #GrowWithUs**
We have already chosen our sourcing channels for this recruitment and kindly ask not to be contacted by any advertisement agents, recruitment agencies or staffing companies.
  
  
  
  
Nouryon is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

* Develop, implement, and monitor quality improvement and health equity work plans.
* Monitor organizational performance measures and identify opportunities for improvement in quality, health outcomes, and equitable access to services.

* Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management for assigned staff.
* Promote a culture of continuous quality improvement, accountability, innovation, and health equity.

* Five (5) years of experience in managed care, healthcare quality, utilization management, care management, population health, compliance, clinical operations, or related healthcare programs.
* Two (2) or more years of program, project, or operational leadership experience supporting quality, regulatory, performance improvement, or healthcare initiatives.
* Three (3) years of progressive leadership, management, or supervisory experience.
* Experience leading quality improvement, clinical operations, regulatory compliance, accreditation, or performance improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing cross-functional projects and organizational initiatives.

* Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures, corrective action plans, quality initiatives, and operational improvement strategies.
* Strong project management, analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with physicians, executive leadership, providers, health equity leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.

Preference will be given to candidates who are local to Imperial, California, but remote candidates living in California will also be considered.

records.title: Head of Technical Operations (Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field)

postedPay.title: Head of Technical Operations (Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field)

records.description:
**About Tutor**
---------------

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**
------------

As Head of Technical Operations, you’ll own manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations. We build hundreds of robots a year today and need to build a lot more. You’ll own how we get there, including the teams, suppliers and facilities, and work closely with engineering along the way.

You’ll report to the CTO. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* Scaling production from hundreds of robots a year to many more
* Manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations
* The teams, suppliers and facilities behind production
* A close partnership with engineering

**Requirements**
----------------

* Ran manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
* Built an operations function and hired the people who run it
* Been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
* Sets clear targets and hires well
* Comfortable on a factory floor

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
* Experience with contract manufacturers
* Experience with quality systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Compensation Range: $250K - $350K

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

Pay: $130,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

* How many years of practical experience do you have with concepts such as six sigma and lean manufacturing?
